Subject: Awareness: Radio Equipment Directive (RED)
Body:
Radio Equipment Directive (RED)

What is RED-DA?

RED-DA is a Delegated Act under the Radio Equipment Directive (RED) that establishes mandatory security measures for radio devices within specific categories or classes. These measures aim to protect networks, user privacy, and prevent fraud.

Starting August 1, 2025, additional rules will apply to wireless devices in the EU market and these rules aim to:

*	Protect networks from security threats.
*	Safeguard user privacy and personal data.
*	Prevent fraud and unauthorized access.

Who does this affect?
Any company that makes, sells, or imports wireless devices to the EU region, must ensure compliance with these new requirements defined in RED-DA.

How to Comply?

Manufacturers shall follow harmonized standards (such as the EN 18031 series) to meet the requirements smoothly. If the governance body in the EU-region conveys that the product should go through certification by a notified body, then such products get certified before being launched in the market.

Need for RED-DA

*	To ensure the security and reliability of wireless devices.
*	To safeguard the users’ personal data from misuse (including childcare, toys, and wearables).
*	To mitigate the risk of financial loss from cyber fraud and hacking.

This regulation being mandatory for anything sold in the market from 1st August 2025, it is crucial to analyze your products for relevance now. CSO-Org has already reached out to the product owners based on the PIF database. In case the products in your domain is RED-DA relevant, do reach out to CSO - VIRT_RO-IN  <mailto:VIRT_RO-IN%20%3cRBEI.ProVIRT@bcn.bosch.com%3e?subject=Need%20support%20on%20RED-DA%20Assessment>  ASAP.

More details, see here <https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/display/SG/EU+Radio+Equipment+Directive+-+Delegated+Act+Cybersecurity>

Microsoft Teams

The Migration from Skype for Business to Microsoft Teams is completed

[Other languages <https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/x/U4ImiQ> ]
 
Dear Microsoft Teams user,
Congratulations! Your Skype for Business (SfB) has been successfully migrated to Microsoft Teams.
 
You will receive the following benefits:
*	Unified communication experience, stay on one tool for chats, calls and meetings.
*	Running with one tool leads to better computer performance and better call experience. 
*	Less distraction by reducing multi-communication tools.
*	As a central hub for collaboration, besides the basic features, Teams also enables centralized access to conversations, files, notes and tasks. The convenience of integrated tools and apps, which you are already using, in one interface makes your day-to-day work more productive. 
 
Please consider the following points:
*	If you still have SfB meetings in your calendar and you are the organizer, please replace the invitation by Teams meetings via Outlook. Further information. <https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=1325189237#Meetings&Calls-ScheduledMeetings/Conferences(OutlookAdd-In)> 
*	Personal call behavior settings like group calls or call forwarding to voicemail need to be adjusted by you. Further information. <https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/display/NGW/Teams+Public+Telephony#TeamsPublicTelephony-WorkwithTeamsPublicTelephony> 
*	You can collaborate with your external partner who is also using Microsoft Teams with the Federation feature. Further information. <https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/x/zQq1dQ> 
 
Do you need support?
*	Support for Bosch employees: For further support, you can access the IT Service Portal <https://rb-servicecatalog.apps.intranet.bosch.com/RequestCenter/website/Grunt/application/index.html> , in the support section you can initiate an instant chat or open a ticket.
*	Support for BSH employees: For further support, you can contact BSH Servicedesk <http://servicedesk.bshg.com/>  and create a service call.
 
We hope you enjoy the new journey with Teams!
 
Your feedback <https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/display/NGW/Teams+in+General#TeamsinGeneral-MicrosoftTeamsFeedback>  counts! - Share your opinion about Microsoft Teams
 
 
Best regards, 
your digital workplace team

Welcome to BGSW!

To ensure that all new team members are well-versed in our Information Security policies and practices, we are organizing a mandatory Information Security Awareness session.

Session 1: 29th April 2025 | 03:00 PM – 04:00 PM IST

Introduction to Information Security

Company Security Policies and Procedures

Best Practices for Data Protection

Q&A Session

Thank you for your cooperation and attention to this important matter. We look forward to your active participation in the session.

Subject: ISP Awareness mail - Clear desk policy, disposal of storage media and hard copies
Body:
Dear All,

 

Here are a few pointers on clear desk policy, disposal of storage media and hard copies.

 



 

 

 

Would we leave our home open, as in the picture on the left? Of course not! Then why would we do it at work?

At Bosch sites, there are many incidents that can be traced back to non-compliance with the Clear Desk rules.

Here, we believe that a clear desk fosters clear thinking. It's not about being a genius—it's about creating an environment where focus and productivity can thrive. After all, work flows best when clutter is kept at bay.

In addition to loss of business benefits, non-compliance with the clear desk policy can result in:

*  Cybersecurity risks

*  Data security risks

*  Physical security risks

To help prevent these risks, we would like to remind you to:

*                 Secure your laptop and hardware with an anti-theft cable or even better, store them in a locker

*                 Lock IT end devices when you are away from them. 

*	Identify and store all confidential documents and data media (CSC2, CSC3, personal data) securely, ensuring they are never left unattended. 
*	Minimize hard copies and dispose them off securely using designated shredders. Collect printouts of C-SC2 or C-SC3 documents promptly from the printer to safeguard sensitive information from unauthorized exposure.
*	Erase C-SC2 and C-SC3 data on digital storage devices Irretrievably before disposal or reuse of the devices. Disposal must be carried out by the responsible department.
*	Never leave your Bosch ID card unattended, do not write any passwords on paper and do not leave any notes with passwords on your desks.

 

 

 

If you have comments or information on this topic, please contact the ISP Partner responsible for your area.

 

For more information on storage media, refer BD storage guidelines <https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=2807858543>  .

 

Security is in our common interest!

 

 

 


 

 


​ 

 

Best regards,

Subject: ISP and CS Awareness: AI Regulations and Responsible AI
Body:
What is AI? 

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is the capability of a machine to imitate intelligent human behavior. It involves creating systems or programs that can perform tasks typically requiring human intelligence, such as learning, problem-solving, language understanding, and decision-making.

What is EU AI Act?

The EU Artificial Intelligence Act <https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/>  (AI Act) is the world’s first comprehensive AI regulations, setting a global precedent like GDPR for data privacy. The regulations defined need to be considered during conception, development, and post deployment of AI systems. While fostering innovations, the main objective is to ensure the safety and trustworthiness of AI systems and protect the rights of the citizens. Responsible AI is not only about compliance but also about fostering public trust and social acceptance of AI technologies.

Towards this the EU AI Act promotes:

*	Design systems that are ethically sound, explainable, and non-discriminatory.
*	Ensure fairness, transparency, robustness, and respect for human autonomy.
*	Continuously monitor and assess AI behavior, updating systems to minimize risks over time.
*	Train AI developers and users in ethical practices and risk mitigation.

The Act’s goals are to:
• Prevent human oversight and have accountability.
• Prevent discriminatory, manipulative, or dangerous AI uses.
• Protect citizens’ privacy, rights, and freedoms.
• Foster trustworthy and innovative AI across the EU and beyond.

To Comply organizations (like Bosch) must:
• Classify their AI system’s risk level (risks like social scoring, scraping of facial images, emotion recognition at workplace, real time remote biometric identification,..)  
• Document system design and functionality thoroughly.
• Implement transparency, security, and human oversight measures.
• Conformity Assessments for high risk. 

• Monitor post-market performance of AI systems and report incidents (if any).

The EU AI Act has a phased implementation:

*	February 2, 2025: Ban on prohibited AI practices starts to apply.
*	August 2, 2025: Rules on general-purpose AI systems with transparency requirements apply to new models.
*	August 2, 2026: Obligations for high-risk AI systems (listed in Annex III of the Act) start to apply.
*	August 2, 2027: Obligations for high-risk AI systems that are products or safety components of products (listed in Annex I of the Act) start to apply. Providers of GPAI models placed on the market before August 2, 2025, have until this date to comply.

Overview of EU AI Act and US AI regulations:

Aspect

European Union (EU) - AI Act

United States (US) - AI Regulation

Approach

Comprehensive and Single law

Fragmented, multi-agency, multi-state

Key Law/Framework

EU Artificial Intelligence Act

Executive Orders, State Laws, Agency Guidelines

Risk Classification

Yes (Unacceptable, High, Limited Risk)

No formal risk classification (sector and issue-specific)

Scope

Global (applies if AI affects EU residents)

Domestic focus with sector-specific measures

Compliance Requirements

Mandatory risk classification, documentation, transparency, conformity assessment, reporting

Varies and depends on agency rules (e.g., FTC, EEOC) or state laws (e.g., NYC bias audits)

Ethical Framework

Trustworthy AI, Human Rights, Privacy - binding

AI Bill of Rights (Blueprint) — non-binding

Enforcement

Centralized EU oversight bodies + Member States

Decentralized (FTC, DOJ, state authorities)

Sector-Specific Rules

High-risk sectors like healthcare, employment, critical infrastructure

Sector-driven (healthcare, education, defense, etc.)

Influence Goal

A global reference for other countries

-

Here are some Do’s & Don’ts to remember with respect to information and data security while using AI modules:


Do's:


1.	Do Verify Information: Always double-check the information provided by AI, especially if it’s important.
2.	Do Use AI for Learning: AI can be a great tool for learning new things, from languages to technical skills.
3.	Do Be Aware of Privacy: Make sure you understand how your data is being used and stored by AI applications.
4.	Do Keep Updated: AI technology is constantly evolving. Stay informed about the latest developments and updates.


Don’ts:


1.	Do not Rely Solely on AI: AI is a tool to assist, not replace human judgment. Always use your own critical thinking.
2.	Do not Share Sensitive Information: Avoid sharing personal or sensitive information with AI tools unless Bosch provided (like Ask Bosch).
3.	Do not Ignore Ethical Concerns: Be mindful of the ethical implications of using AI, such as bias and fairness.
4.	Do not Overuse AI: Balance the use of AI with human interaction to avoid becoming overly dependent on technology.

Don’t Assume AI is Perfect: 

*	AI can make mistakes. 
*	Always review and verify its outputs.
*	Aware of Intellectual Property (Copyright Infringement, Ownership of output and Data privacy violations)

Subject: ISP-CS Awareness: Cyber Resilience Act (CRA)
Body:
🛡️ EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) | EU Regulation 2024/2847 |

✅ What is the CRA?

The Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) is a regulation introduced by the European Union and adopted on 10th October 2024, to ensure mandatory cybersecurity for all hardware and software products with digital elements throughout their lifecycle.

🔍 Why CRA?

*	📈 Rise in cyberattacks targeting small businesses and critical infrastructure 
*	🛡️ Protect consumers and businesses by ensuring secure digital products through patching

🔍 Scope: 

In-scope

Out-of-scope

Digital (B2B or B2C)

Medical devices (MDR and IVDR regulation covers)

software & hardware products

vehicles and components (UNR 155 and UNR156 cover)

Product manufacturers, importers, distributors, FOSS representatives.

spare parts

Vehicles for agriculture and offroad

open-source software without any commercial activity

⚙️ Key Requirements:

*	✔️ Essential cybersecurity requirements for all digital products.
*	🚨 Additional requirements for critical products.
*	🔁 Mandatory patch updates during expected product use to be done for free.
*	🕒 24-month transition period for compliance. (effective Aug-2027)
*	💰 Penalties for non-compliance: Up to €15 million or 2.5% of global turnover (whichever is higher).

🌍 Impact of CRA on One-BGSW:

*	Applies to digital offerings (both legacy and new) targeted to EU region: 

	*	global customers (iTraMS, Flashing Solutions, ..)
	*	within Bosch (like prOSSec, Fosslens, DeviceBridge,..)

Further Reference:

EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) - C/CYG - Cybersecurity - Docupedia <https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=2431659859>

Body:
Dear all,

 

Hope you are doing good.

 

Since the weather conditions are not good in Pune location many Apprentices are falling sick. To avoid further damage we would like to make the training online for the next 3 days.

 

You may exercise discretion and choose whether to work from the office or remotely from Wed till Fri (28-30 May) and attend the online training.

 

Ensure that you are attending the online training, attendance will be marked.

 

You have to resume to office on 2nd June for the In-person training 

 

Thank you

 

Regards

Sandhya

Subject: Staying Safe and Flexible This Week | BGSW Pune Associates 

 

 

Dear Team,

 

We hope you are safe and staying dry.

 

Due to the ongoing rainfall and alerts in effect for Pune, we understand that commuting may be challenging and potentially unsafe. 

In light of this, we are temporarily relaxing the Smart Hybrid Policy for the remainder of this week. Till Friday, May 30, employees may exercise discretion and choose whether to work from the office or remotely. 

There will be no requirement to meet the usual 4-day onsite attendance during this period for associates working out of Pune.

 

We trust you to make the best decision based on your local conditions and personal safety. 

We know you’ll continue to support your teams and keep things moving, as you always do.

 

We will continue to monitor the situation and keep you informed of any further updates.

 

Stay safe and take care.

Best Regards,

BGSW Pune

Subject: ISP Awareness : Labelling of information at Bosch
Body:
Envelopes marked "Confidential" may sound like something from a James Bond movie. But labelling is an important — and in many cases mandatory — practice in Bosch. Why? Because it makes us aware of the need to specially protect specific information.

	

How must information be labelled?


When we talk about "labeling" in Bosch, we are referring to the requirement to clearly mark "Confidential" and "Strictly Confidential" data as such. You can find more information below on how to achieve proper labeling: 

 

Confidentiality level

How to label?

Public
(C-SC0)

SC0, can be labelled as "Public", "Press Release" or "Publication" Ex: Newsletters, Bosch websites, brochures

Internal 
(C-SC1)

Business information is by default considered "internal" unless otherwise required or indicated

Confidential 
(C-SC2)

Examples of how to label:

*	Documents marked or stamped "Confidential" on the first page (default option)
*	Envelopes marked "Confidential".
*	Email subject line marked with "Confidential" or included in main text (must be encrypted)
*	Files can include "Confidential" in their filename.
*	Folders could include "Confidential" in their folder name (but beware of labelling if the confidential files are later moved or sent)
*	Specific systems could be used for storage, if the specific systems imply a certain security classification, e.g. SAP, HR Global (but beware of labelling if the confidential files are later moved or sent)

Strictly Confidential 
(C-SC3)

Examples of how to label:

*	Documents marked or stamped "Strictly Confidential" on every page (default option)
*	Envelopes marked "Strictly Confidential" (within an unmarked envelope)
*	Email subject line marked with "Strictly Confidential", or this is included in the main text (must be encrypted)
*	Files can include "Strictly Confidential" in their filename.
*	Folders could include "Strictly Confidential" in their folder name (but beware of labelling if the confidential files are later moved or sent)
*	Specific systems could be used for storage, if the specific systems imply a certain security classification, e.g. SAP, HR Global (but beware of labelling if the confidential files are later moved or sent)

	
	If labelling is impossible

Alternate options are allowed. Specifically, labelling is not required in either of the following situations:

	*	If the security class can be clearly derived from the storage location/IT system.

Ex: Confidential information could be placed in an access restricted “Share Point on Premises” folder named “CONFIDENTIAL”.

	*	Documents in applications (e.g., SAP, HR-Global), as long as the documents remain within the application.

In Bosch, it is mandatory for all departments to maintain an information classification, also known as a “Data concept”. This is an overview of information types and their respective security class. Ask your manager if you do not know where this overview is, with which the users can know if the information is “confidential” or not.

	
	
As always, if you have any doubts and still any questions about how to label confidential information, remember to contact the ISP Partner <https://rb-wam.bosch.com/my-isp/en/#/>  appointed in your area.

	
			

 

 

 

 

Best regards,

#TribePune | World Environment Day: CSR Initiative - Supporting Local Farmers with Sustainable Planting

On June 7th, to mark World Environment Day, #TribePune organized a CSR initiative focused on sustainable agriculture and rural support. Volunteers spent the day in a nearby village planting a diverse mix of climate-resilient seeds including custard apple, karanj, chich (tamarind), amla, hirda, arjun plain, and mahogany. These native species were selected for their ecological suitability and long-term value, supporting both reforestation and future income for local farmers.

This initiative aimed to strengthen rural livelihoods while promoting environmental stewardship. Volunteers not only contributed their time and energy but also built meaningful connections with the community. By supporting sustainable planting, the event offered a practical way to give back to nature and invest in the economic resilience of local farmers—making World Environment Day truly impactful.


 


 





Leadership Connect with Shruthi Shivaswamy: A SheRise Moment at #ManaHyderabad

On June 5th, SheRise Community at BGSW #ManaHyderabad hosted an inspiring Leadership Connect session with ShruthiShivaswamy, Department Head, MS/EBB-ETAS and MS/ECT-ETAS, as part of the.

Shruthi shared her leadership journey with honesty and heart—offering valuable insights on navigating challenges, embracing growth, and leading with authenticity. Associates engaged in a meaningful conversation on career building, confidence, and creating space for women to rise and thrive in tech.

A powerful reminder that when women support women, incredible things happen. 💪🌟


 


 








Exploring SDV Trends & Success Stories at #ManaHyderabad 🚗💡         

Last week, we had the pleasure of hosting Niranjan Babu, Technical Director at NE-ETAS, for an engaging session on “Overview of SDV Trends and Acquisition Success Stories.” Held on 10th June, the session offered rich insights into the evolving landscape of Software-Defined Vehicles, OEM expectations, and ongoing initiatives in the IN-region.

Targeted at our senior associates, the session sparked meaningful conversations and provided a strategic perspective on industry transformations. A big thank you to Niranjan and everyone who joined and contributed to the dialogue!

Blood Donation Drive at BGSW #ManaHyderabad 

This week, our BGSW Hyderabad family came together for a life-saving cause — the Blood Donation Camp, and the response was truly heartwarming! 💪

✨ 125 associates volunteered to donate, and we’re proud to share that 103 successful donations were made — a remarkable effort that will go a long way in saving lives.

A huge shoutout to Krishna Potta Vamsi (SDS/ECE-CE) and our volunteers @Kothapalli Jacob, @Sateesh Babu Maddirala, @Siringi Sowmya Selsi, and @Durga Praneetha Appana for their full-day support and dedication. 🙌 This wouldn't have been possible without your efforts!

Introducing Legistify: Bosch India's New Litigation Management Tool



                                                      

Dear Boschlers,

C/LSR-IN goes DIGITAL!

C/LSR-IN is happy to share it’s brand-new digital tool “Legistify”. Implementation of this comprehensive litigation management tool marks another milestone towards our journey of digitalization.



What is Legistify?

Legistify is a state-of-the-art legal tech platform specifically designed to streamline litigation processes, improve case tracking, and enhance overall legal workflow efficiency. The platform offers a centralized repository for all litigation-related information, enabling better coordination and knowledge sharing. This tool would also support due diligence activities in Compliance and M&A projects.







Key Benefits for Bosch India Litigation Team:

*	Case Management: Access all litigation information in one secure platform.
*	Enhanced Tracking & Reporting: Real-time updates and comprehensive analytics on case progress.
*	Improved Collaboration: Seamless communication between internal teams and external counsel.
*	Document Management: Secure storage and easy retrieval of all legal documents.





Advancing Digital Transformation in Legal Operations

*	Enables a shift from manual to data-driven legal operations
*	Supports smarter decision-making with real-time analytics
*	Enhances due diligence for Compliance and M&A projects
*	Boosts efficiency across litigation workflows
*	Aligns with Bosch’s broader digital innovation strategy

Subject: ISP Awareness | Social Engineering incident
Body:
Picture this: You are relaxing on a Sunday in your shared accommodation. An individual (X) claiming to be a Bosch associate approaches you with the request to use your laptop to complete an important presentation for the next day. You refuse initially, knowing that it is not permitted by the ISP (information security and data protection) policy to share login credentials. However, continuous pleading by X evokes your sympathy and you share the laptop after logging in, i.e., in logged-in condition. X works in your presence and finishes the task. All is well that ends well, right?

Wrong!! You intuitively check your laptop and find that some internal data has been accessed and mailed to the personal mail-ID of X. Finding this to be suspicious, you inform your manager, only to know that the individual is an ex-associate! Reality hits – you have just been a victim of a Social Engineering attack!

Social Engineering is a manipulation technique aimed at tricking individuals into revealing sensitive information, carrying out actions they wouldn’t normally perform, or making decisions contrary to their usual behavior. Social engineering attacks are strategies used by malicious individuals to take advantage of human psychology and persuade people to compromise their security or privacy.

Always keep in mind:

*	Never share your Bosch resource (e.g., laptop) in logged-in condition : Sharing a laptop in ‘logged-in’ condition is the same as leaving it unattended or sharing your password and gives others access to accounts and information that you are authorized to access.
*	Never share your credentials (user id and password) with anybody. If somebody asks you to do so – remind them that they are not supposed to ask for it as per the ISP policy.
*	Be vigilant: Be cautious of “urgent task completion” requests, especially if the request is persistent. This could be the warning bell of a Social Engineering attack. Contact your manager and your ISP Partner immediately to report any such incidents.

Access control tips:

*	Review File Share access periodically: Review the File Shares periodically for access (e.g., AIM check, CARDIO, etc.) to prevent unauthorized access.
*	Review Distribution Lists periodically: Since access is provided to many of the resources such as File Share and Docupedia through Distribution Lists, it is necessary to review the Distribution Lists also periodically.
*	Selection of proper storage channels: File Share supports access restriction up to a maximum of level 3 folder. In case of a requirement for access restriction beyond level 3 folder, please look for alternative BD-provided solution such as SharePoint.

Remember: Information security is everyone's responsibility. By staying vigilant and following these guidelines, we can help protect Bosch's valuable assets.

	Pre-Go-live Information of Travel Settlement via GS Service Platform

June 2025



   In Short:

*	The BGSW Travel Settlement mailbox will be deactivated, and
	all inquiries will be managed through the GS Service Platform (ESM)
*	Go-Live Date: June 24, 2025.
*	Your primary contact for support request will be GS Service Platform
*	Training dates for using the new ticketing tool 

________________________________

Dear Users,

We would like to inform you as user from BGSW entity that you should use GS Service Platform (ESM) <https://gbs.bosch.com/>  from the 24th June 2025 for all travel settlement related inquiries (applicable only for BGSW entity).

 <https://gbs.bosch.com/esc?id=emp_taxonomy_topic&topic_id=153e38041b9041106b8efd149b4bcb3d&in_context=true> 

	

 

 

 

 

 

 

	What …?

The primary channel for you to submit the inquiries will be the GS Service Platform (ESM) <https://gbs.bosch.com/> , as the BGSW Travel Settlement option will be switched off.

 <https://gbs.bosch.com/esc?id=emp_taxonomy_topic&topic_id=153e38041b9041106b8efd149b4bcb3d&in_context=true> 

	

 

 

 

 

 

 

	Why …?

Submitting a ticket via the GS Service Portal ensures a higher quality support and allows our agents to respond faster. 

You will have the possibility to accept or reject a proposed resolution and to provide valuable feedback.

All this will lead to an improved and faster support.

 

 <https://gbs.bosch.com/esc?id=emp_taxonomy_topic&topic_id=153e38041b9041106b8efd149b4bcb3d&in_context=true> 

	

 

 

 

 

 

 

	How …?

From 24th June 2025 you can go to the platform and raise your request directly via the template.

Comprehensive training sessions will be conducted to familiarize you with the new system. The sessions are designed to provide you with the necessary knowledge to effectively use the new system.

Subject: The Weekly Wrap 20th June 2025
Body:
20th June 2025


 



 <https://forms.office.com/e/bRfGnimUsb> 


 


 





BGSW at GCC 2025 Round Table Summit on 
“From Data to Delight”

BGSW was glad to be part of the recently organized GCC Round Table Summit on “From Data to Delight” - where the conversation went far beyond data pipelines and platforms. 

Mr. Guruprasad S. (Vice President, Multi Market Business Sectors) together with Mr. Shankar Datta M S H (Practice Leader, Data Life Cycle Management) were invited to share their insights and views. 

The forum explored how GCCs are reshaping data architectures to enable enterprise-wide interoperability, AI-native agility, and real-time intelligence. BGSW Multimarket delegates shared information about DataNexus, a metadata-driven platform that unifies data at scale, accelerates time-to-insight, and the recently won the Finkelstein Award for Data Engineering Innovation.

The discussions delved into Re-architecting for AI Readiness, Data-Driven approaches to foster new innovations, Interoperability & Data Collaboration, federated data models, compliance, and ethical frameworks.


 


 






Sustainability Tribe - World Environment Day

On June 5th, Tribe of sustainability, MS/EMH (MS/NE-PG) & GR/FCM1-BGSW came together across BANGALORE, COIMBATORE, and PUNE to celebrate World Environment Day 2025. 

🌱 Under the UN global theme #BeatPlasticPollution, the event was a powerful reminder of our collective commitment to sustainability—through innovation, awareness, and purpose-driven action.

In line with Bosch’s sustainability focus—Climate Action, Circular Economy, Water, Health, Diversity, and Human Rights—this initiative reinforced the need to embed sustainability into everything we do.

The Tribe of Sustainability initiated by MS/EMH is a Bosch engineer-led community focused on embedding Eco-conscious thinking into our technologies, sourcing strategies, and innovation processes. From CO₂ reduction to material efficiency and plastic waste mitigation, the Tribe embodies Bosch’s “Invented for life” ethos.

What began in 2024 as a small, passionate initiative—with little idea of how far it would go—has now grown into a powerful movement that is creating real value for the organization.

Under the leadership of Sudhir Vijay Sattigeri (MS/EMH), our team took great pride in driving this initiative across BGSW—leading efforts in Design for Environment, Product Carbon Footprint, and sustainable material solutions that pave the way for responsible innovation.

Today, we’re proud, inspired, and more motivated than ever to accelerate our journey and launch even more initiatives that contribute to a greener, more sustainable future.

We were honored by the presence and insights of our senior leadership in BGSW and Bosch, India:

Guru Mallikarjuna (MS/BE3 MS/NE-PS PS-SC/CE-AP), Hegde Shrikanth P (MS/NE-PG MS/KAM-ME), Balaji Ramalingam (BGSW/ETX), Shashi Kumar B S (GR/FCM-Ban1), Aravind Maiya (RBIN/FCM GR/FCM-IN GR/PPR-IN), Paladhi Amit Kumar (C/SEE-IN RBIN/HSE-Ban), Padmanabhan Kannan (GR/FCM-BGSW BGSW/PSO), Murali Ramalingam (GR/FCM1-BGSW), Narayan Naved (MS/NE-ES, Center Head-Cob)

Market place that brought our sustainability efforts to life:

🟢 Stall 1 – MS/EMH; Design for Environment & PCF; 

🟣 Stall 2 – MS/ENH; Plastic CoC & Additive Manufacturing

Full OBDonUDS implementation for customer- Volkswagen (VW)

MS/EPV41-PS team is proud to share the success story of OBDonUDS delivery to our customer, Volkswagen.

CW22’ 2025 has been a remarkable week for the EA211 NAR project as the delivery of the OBDonUDS feature was successfully delivered to VW. This is the first project to deliver OBDonUDS feature as part of the Engine Control Unit (ECU) software to the customer. By now, some might wonder what OBDonUDS is!

On-Board Diagnostics over Unified Diagnostic Services (OBDonUDS) is the successor to the OBD-II standard (Society of Automotive Engineers (SAE) J1979). 

It's a communication protocol that uses UDS, a well-established standard for manufacturer-specific diagnostics, to enable more comprehensive vehicle diagnostics. OBDonUDS offers enhanced capabilities, including Diagnostic Trouble Code (DTC) based readiness, extended data records for DTCs, and snapshot support for DTCs. Close to 450 Software components are updated to develop this feature in the ECU software.

Structured planning, Ontime Problem Solving and Great Team spirit played a vital role in the Feature Development. Seamless coordination within various Function Teams across locations in India, Vienna, Cluj, Vietnam, Germany and Calibration Teams in Germany helped to achieve the successful delivery of this feature to the customer.

Several challenges like Memory Overflow, Runtime Issue, etc. were encountered and got solved by the experts from the team on time. Volkswagen will use the ECU with the OBDonUDS features in their EVO2 Engine family Vehicles starting 2027. 

This is a true testament of team’s capability in handling complex projects from India and wouldn’t have been possible without continued support from Prasanna B (MS/EPV4-PS) and Murali Narasimhan (MS/EPV-PS), throughout the feature development and delivery.


 


 








XC-Converse         

On June 11th, 2025, we hosted the second XC - Converse of the year, attended by over 50 participants in person and more than 20 online. A highlight was the presence of Dyrbusch Damian, our Key Account Manager(NE-XC), who shared insights on growth and strategic execution. Business updates included the first Standard Operating Procedure for Suzuki DA3 and a revenue report of 1.6 billion EUR for CE-02. Bringing Movement to the Workplace: A Desk-tastic Wellness Experience

On June 17th and 18th, associates across BGSW embraced movement and mindfulness through the org-wide wellness initiative Desk-tastic Yoga Day.

This energizing event offered a much-needed pause from the daily hustle, helping participants de-stress, recharge and elevate their fitness, all without leaving their desks! Led by 11 expert instructors from cult.fit, and supported by our enthusiastic BGSW volunteers, the sessions featured simple, accessible yoga stretches and breathing techniques perfect for work breaks or between meetings.

What made it special? The focus on easy-to-do, chair-friendly routines meant that everyone from yoga newbies to regular practitioners could participate and benefit.

The outcome? A wave of refreshed minds, revitalized bodies, and a renewed commitment to workplace wellness. Desk-tastic Yoga Day wasn't just about fitness — it was a reminder that even micro-breaks can make a macro difference.

Here’s to moving more, stressing less, and making every stretch count!                                                                                                                 


 


 








#TribePune | Brewing Insights: A Coffee Conversation with NE1-XC Leadership         

The NE1-XC Pune team recently engaged in a virtual coffee conversation with leadership duo Mujumdar Gopinath Raghavendra, Vice President, Engineering XC, and Saravanan Sathish Babu, Director, Talent Management.

Amid industry challenges, this session provided a platform for experience sharing, business hurdles and opportunities, and the role of associates in shaping the future. 

Leadership highlighted the impact of R&D costs on securing new business, emphasizing cost efficiency through smart work and innovation.

For young professionals, the key takeaway was: "Horizontal knowledge is essential—one should be open to learning new technologies."

Ultimately, this exchange strengthened the bond between leadership and teams, fostering resilience and innovation, while embracing the mindset of being Bold, Boundaryless, and Proud—equipping the NE1-XC Pune family to navigate challenges with confidence.

#TribePune | Limitless Learning Session 5: Making “Working Smart” a Reality 

“Limitless Learning" is an initiative driven at BGSW Pune and is led by the Learning and Development team. Associates actively participate in sharing knowledge, fostering a culture of continuous learning and growth.The fifth session of the Limitless Learning series was led by Aakanksha Tiwari (BGSW/ADM-CSR1), CSR Lead at BGSW Pune, who hosted a highly engaging and insightful session titled “Work Smart: Mastering Time Management, Prioritization & Deadlines.”

Drawing from real workplace challenges, Aakanksha walked participants through practical frameworks like the Eisenhower Matrix and the ABCDE Method, helping everyone understand the difference between what’s urgent and what’s important.

The session stood out for its interactive format, relatable examples, and down-to-earth tips like time blocking, the Pomodoro Technique, and the Two-Minute Rule. These weren’t just theories—they were tools people could start using right away. What made the biggest impact? Each participant walked away with a personalized action plan to manage their time more effectively and reduce stress. The feedback said it all—words like “eye-opening,” “immediately useful,” and “practical” came up again and again.

Thanks to Aakanksha’s thoughtful approach, this session turned big ideas into simple, actionable steps. “Work smart” isn’t just a buzzword anymore—it’s something we’re all better equipped to do.

Subject: Speak up! We listen. | World Whistleblowing Day 2025
Body:
In recognition of World Whistleblowing Day on June 23, we want to highlight the significance of reporting potential Compliance violations and answering key questions about whistleblowing.

 

What is a possible Compliance violation? 

A violation exists if the Compliance Requirement is not fulfilled. A Compliance Requirement is an obligation to adhere to all legally binding external laws, the  <https://bgn.bosch.com/FIRSTspiritWeb/permlink/wcms_c_-about-EN> Code of Conduct, and all other internal regulations when doing business for the Bosch Corporate Group. 

 

Why should I report a possible Compliance violation? 

Reporting potential Compliance violations at Bosch is crucial because it safeguards the company, your colleagues, and yourself. By speaking up, you help avert potential harm, maintain our commitment to legal and ethical conduct, and protect Bosch's reputation.

 

What does protection of reporting persons mean? 

Bosch is committed to protecting reporting persons from all forms of discrimination on account of a report made in good faith. Any retaliation due to such a report is prohibited.

 

How do I report a possible Compliance violation?  
Associates can contact their immediate supervisors, the central Compliance organization (C/CM), or the legal department (C/LS). At Bosch we have the following channels to report possible violations of the Compliance Requirement: 

*	Whistleblowing system Speak up!:  <https://www.bkms-system.net/bosch-compliance> https://www.bkms-system.net/bosch-compliance
*	Reporting Office: Robert Bosch GmbH, Compliance Management C/CMI, 
Postbox 10 60 50, 70049 Stuttgart (Germany)
*	Email to the BGSW Compliance Officer: Narottam Kumar (C/CMR-BGSW-IN)

 

You can use Speak up! to contact the Compliance Organization and provide reports at any time, 24/7. The Speak up! platform can be reached through BGN or the internet. You can also use Speak up! to report anonymously. 

 

More information is available in Bosch GlobalNet:  <https://bos.ch/speakup> bos.ch/speakup. 

 

Best regards,

C/CMR-BGSW-IN

BGSW Marketing and Communications

Subject: Form-16 for the financial year 2024-2025 is now available
Body:
Dear Associates,

 

Form-16 (the certificate of earnings and tax deduction) for associates relating to the financial year April 2024 - March 2025 (also referred to as Assessment Year 2025-2026) is available as digitally signed PDF documents (PDF)as per below:

 

*	Part A – Statement generated from TRACES portal (administered by the Indian Income tax department) **

** Part A of Form-16 will be available only for those associates for whom there was income tax deduction from their Indian payroll during the period April 2024 – Mar 2025 

*	Part B – Statement of earnings and tax computation – Generated from TRACES portal (administered by the Indian Income tax department)

 

Associates may also note that their name & address in Part-A & Part-B is as per the database of the Government of India (Income tax department) based on the PAN application submitted by the associates. Any inconsistencies in the name in Part-A & Part-B need to be addressed as a correction as per the defined process by the Income tax department. BGSW does not have any control on how the name is displayed in both Part-A & Part-B.

*	Part B Annexure – Statement of other exemptions, deductions & details of perquisites (issued by BGSW)

To access the Form-16, associates have to login at:

 

Employee Services -> Associate Applications -> Form-16 -> Year 2024-2025

 

The digitally signed Form-16 document can be downloaded by associates for any of their requirements. Associates need to preserve this document as part of their personal docket for any of their requirements in the future.

 

Kindly clear your browser’s cache and cookies before opening Form 16 to avoid errors.

 

FILING OF INCOME TAX RETURNS

 

Please note that as per the income tax rule, last date for filing individual tax returns is September 15, 2025

 

Associates can file their Income tax returns online at https://www.incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal

 

Queries / Clarifications on the Form-16 issued.

 

Associates who need any clarifications on the Form-16 issued may contact the Income Tax helpdesk by raising SSF ticket <https://inside.bosch.com/irj/portal?NavigationTarget=navurl%3A%2F%2F334c4e872d0993099e373657c8f8b8c8>  – Use Subject: Form 16 Query – “Short Subject”.

 

     Associates on deputation can contact as per their location SPOC underlined below:

 

·              Associates at Bangalore location : external.hitesh.j@bosch.com <mailto:external.hitesh.j@bosch.com> 

·              Associates at Pune & Hyderabad location : external.girish.s@bosch.com <mailto:external.girish.s@bosch.com> 

·         Associates at Coimbatore location : external.rahul.v@in.bosch.com <mailto:external.rahul.v@in.bosch.com> 

 

Please note that Form-16 is issued to only those associates who have received Indian Salary from BGSW during the period Apr 2024 to March 2025. 

 

Brief note on the statutory aspects:

As per the Indian Information Technology Act, 2000, signatures in digital mode are considered as valid. 

 

As per the Circular No.2/2007 from the Income Tax Department, the Indian Government has allowed Employers to digitally sign and issue Form-16 certificates to all their associates instead of printed ones. 

 

Digitally signed Form-16 in softcopy format can be used by the associate for any of their personal requirements (e.g..: Bank loan approvals, etc.).

Subject: The Weekly Wrap 27th June 2025
Body:
27th June 2025


 









BGSW in the News         

BGSW Inaugurates Accessible Resource Center (ARC) to Advance Inclusive STEM Education for Visually Impaired Students

BGSW in collaboration with Vision Empower (VE) and the Centre for Accessibility in the Global South (CAGS) at the International Institute of Information Technology, Bangalore (IIITB), has inaugurated the Accessible Resource Center (ARC) - a pioneering inclusive education hub designed to students with visual impairment through assistive technology and special educators empowerment and training program  through a specially curated pedagogy.

As part of BGSW’s CSR commitment to inclusive and sustainable development, ARC is focused on increasing access to quality STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) education for  students with visual impairment in Grades K–10, while building the capacity of special educators to provide effective, technology-enabled instruction.

Read the full media coverage here <https://thecsruniverse.com/articles/bosch-global-software-technologies-inaugurates-center-to-advance-inclusive-stem-education-for-students-with-visual-impairment> 

Navigating the Path to Responsible AI 

On June 18th, BGSW's ISP Office, in collaboration with SX/EDS-MM, hosted an insightful session on Responsible AI, bringing together perspectives on the rapidly evolving AI landscape—from traditional Machine Learning to Generative and Agentic AI.

The session focused on the critical pillars of Responsible AI: Explainability, Compliance, Security, Ethics, Fairness, and Robustness. It highlighted the growing necessity for safeguards to mitigate risks such as bias, misinformation, and unintended behaviors in autonomous systems.

With close to 500 associates joining both in-person and via Teams, the session sparked engaging discussions around real-world AI use cases—such as chatbots, deepfakes, and self-driving cars—and emphasized the need to build trustworthy AI systems that are aligned with human values. The dialogue reinforced the collective responsibility to ensure transparency, accountability, and ethical rigor in every stage of AI development and deployment.


 


 








Fostering Academia – Industry Engagement (Research Advisory Board of RIT)         

The 6th Research Advisory Board meeting of Ramaiah Institute of Technology (RIT), Bangalore was recently held. The advisory board comprises of select academicians, researchers, industry experts, to evaluate and guide RIT’s research initiatives across diverse STEM disciplines. Mr. Guruprasad S. (Vice President and Global Director) has been on this advisory board member (honorary) since many years. Selected work(s) of repute from the institute are presented to the advisory board to seek feedback/suggestions towards shaping a multi-faceted perspective. Presentation during the current round included topics from Data Science, Applied Mathematics, Applied Physics and Material Sciences for application into domains like Aeronautics, Healthcare and Life Sciences. Mr. Guruprasad re-iterated the importance of industry aligned research, innovation that is scalable and commercializing research outcomes through IP by leveraging emerging technological trends. Mr. Deba Prasad Tripathy (Program Director – Industry Vertical) accompanied and shared his perspectives as well.

Bosch and BGSW commitment to foster an inclusive environment for furthering Science and Technology for betterment of life stands as a guiding light in these actions.

SX/NE-MM celebrates Skill University Graduation Day  

The SX/NE-MM Unified Talent Family proudly celebrated its first “Skill University Graduation Day” on June 26th, marking a major milestone in its journey of talent development. This vibrant event honored the achievements of 103 graduates across various skill levels, advancing to next level of proficiency.

Since its launch in August 2024, the program has become a flagship initiative, offering structured learning paths, hands-on training, and rigorous assessments to prepare associates for the evolving tech landscape.

Celebrations took place across all locations Bangalore, Coimbatore, Pune, and Hyderabad, with each location echoing the spirit of unity and shared accomplishment. The multi-location format encouraged broader participation and reinforced the collaborative culture that defines SX/NE-MM.

The atmosphere was filled with pride, enthusiasm, and a sense of achievement. This event was more than a ceremony - it symbolized our collective commitment to continuous learning and growth. The energy and pride displayed by the graduates set a powerful tone for future cohorts and highlighted the long-term impact of the program.

Congratulations to all the graduates and heartfelt thanks to every team member who made this a success!


 


 





Fostering an AI first Culture at MS/ESY-VM

The AI@Product Engineering initiative launched by MS/ESY-VM fosters an AI-first culture. With 60 self-nominated volunteers, the program focuses on building knowledge, value stream mapping, and deploying AI solutions. The initiative emphasizes collaboration, and continuous learning. A defining feature of this initiative is its self-nomination and volunteerism to the program. 

Read more. <https://connect.bosch.com/blogs/978a83a6-7a0d-4e55-a0af-6bd1da6376a8/entry/Fostering_an_AI_first_Culture_at_ESY?lang=en_us> 


 


 








Leading with Agility – ALDP at BGSV-VM         

Agile Leadership Development Program was launched at BGSV to equip leaders with complete know-how on Agile methods to transform their projects. Workshops were organized to cover key aspects of Agile Leadership Characteristics, such as problem-solving, enabling flow, value stream mapping, and creative thinking among others. 

The three-month program (January to April) focuses on having deep understanding and insights of agile principles and how to apply them in projects to foster collaboration, flexibility, and continuous improvement. The program also features how to embrace an agile mindset, facilitate collaboration by breaking down silos, encourage open communication, and deliver value to customers. 

Read more <https://connect.bosch.com/blogs/978a83a6-7a0d-4e55-a0af-6bd1da6376a8/entry/Leading_with_Agility?lang=en_us> .

Streamlining Quality and Efficiency with GitHub Copilot at MS/EBN-VM 

Using GitHub Copilot, variant handling is streamlined by reducing manual effort and speeding up development cycles. This automation ensures consistent vehicle ECU software variants, enhancing scalability and reliability. It highlights AI’s expanding role in boosting productivity and coding accuracy in software development. In the fast-paced world of software development, efficiency, quality, and accuracy are paramount. Recently, in MS/EBN-VM’s development team has implemented variant automation using GitHub Copilot AI, and the results have been transformative. This automation approach has not only saved valuable time but also significantly reduced manual effort, resulting in improved code quality.  

Read more. <https://connect.bosch.com/blogs/978a83a6-7a0d-4e55-a0af-6bd1da6376a8/entry/Streamlining_Quality_and_Efficiency_with_GitHub_Copilot?lang=en_us> 


 


 








Plantation Drive at Namma Special Park         

Ever seen engineers trade laptops for shovels? That’s exactly what happened during our Plantation Drive at Namma Special Park, Kalapatti in February 2025. As part of the WeMatter initiative, 27 green-hearted volunteers dug in (literally) and planted over 180 saplings. Each team channeled their inner gardener, racing against the sun (and each other) to green the space for special children. This wasn’t just an environmental initiative- it symbolized our commitment to inclusivity and community welfare.

Women’s day Celebration- Voices that Inspire 

On March 12, 2025, we celebrated Women’s Day with meaning, laughter, and a few friendly debates! The event kicked off with a fun debate and trust us, no one held back! From “Does women have work-life balance?” to “Should men do the dishes?,” sparks flew (all respectfully, of course). This was followed by a powerful storytelling session spotlighting inspiring women who have broken barriers and built legacies, leaving us teary-eyed and proud. To top it off, we had a surprise appreciation moment where the men stepped up to hand out greeting cards and chocolates to all the amazing women around. It wasn’t just a celebration; it was a heartfelt reminder that empowerment starts with everyday appreciation.


 


 








Cubicle Decoration Day- Creativity at Every Corner         

Who says only Pinterest pros can design pretty spaces? In March 2025, we had Cubicle Decoration Day, our desks got a glow-up! To spark creativity and foster a sense of belonging, we organized a vibrant Cubicle Decoration Day. Teams transformed their workspaces into themed zones using sustainable and colorful materials. The event saw incredible participation, laughter, and bonding as colleagues shared ideas, DIY tips, and stories behind their decor. Judging the spaces was like walking through a live art gallery. Judges evaluated the teams based on creativity, collaboration, and storytelling, turning an ordinary day into an extraordinary celebration of team spirit.

ECD Goals Campaign- Engineering Beyond the Task: #WeFocus@MS/ECD-PS 

To align with our department’s vision, we launched the ECD Goals Campaign in April 2025, turning strategic objectives into something meaningful, memorable, and fun! Through engaging posters and teaser emails, we simplified and spotlighted the core ECD goals and their relevance to our daily work. Associates were encouraged to reflect, interact, and contribute ideas on how they could be part of the growth journey. Adding a creative twist, associates were grouped into teams and invited to present their understanding through skit plays, bringing goals to life with storytelling, humor, and collaboration. The campaign was more than just awareness, it was a reminder that capability building isn’t a one-time task, but a shared, ongoing journey we’re all a part of.


 


 








IMO VCU Project Success Celebration- Steering Through Challenges         

Success isn’t just about delivery- it’s about delivering despite the headwinds. The IMO VCU project team celebrated a well-deserved success meet in April 2025, after achieving a milestone series delivery, overcoming a journey filled with tight timelines and customer escalations. Through late nights, technical hurdles, and high expectations, the team showcased resilience, collaboration, and commitment- proving once again that challenges only bring out the best in us.

The event was facilitated by our Section Head, Mr. Madhusudan K R, who applauded the team’s grit and agility. He also presented awards and appreciation, acknowledging the hard work and collective ownership that turned obstacles into outcomes. The IMO VCU team’s journey stands as a powerful example of how focused execution and team spirit can drive success, even under pressure.

ECD Day- Celebration with a purpose 

May 29, 2025, wasn’t an average Thursday- it was ECD Day, and we turned our workplace into a festival ground. ECD Day 2025 was a perfect mix of celebration, culture, and community spirit. The day kicked off with show-stopping performances form melodious solo singing, soulful group singing, and a high-energy group dance that made even the shyest spectators tap their feet. But we didn’t stop there. The surprise twist? The “Mr. and Mrs. Ethnic” contest- an instant hit that brought out the best of our traditional glam and cheeky charm. Best dressed, best moves, and best smiles- judged, cheered, and Insta-approved! Then came the real crowd-puller: a buzzing CSR fundraising fair with 8 creative stalls ranging from spicy snacks to chic nail art and head-turning mehndi. The real win, though? Every rupee raised went towards stationery kits for children in an orphanage, proving that when engineers celebrate, they do it with purpose.


 


 





MB Team Achieves ASPICE Level 3- Driving Excellence

The MS/ECD-PS MB Team celebrated a significant milestone on April 2025, successfully achieving ASPICE Level 3 in Audit! This accomplishment isn’t just a number; it’s a testament to our engineering maturity, quality mindset, and relentless pursuit of continuous improvement in software and systems development.

The celebration was filled with cheers, smiles, and well-deserved recognition- because every reviewed document, every resolved gap, and every completed checklist led to this proud moment. It was a team effort powered by rigorous process adherence and seamless collaboration. The event 
was graced by our Section Head, Mr. Madhusudan K R, who facilitated the celebration, appreciated the team’s efforts, 
and presented awards to acknowledge the dedication and excellence demonstrated throughout the journey.

We also took time to appreciate and honor our supporting teams including process responsible and function development teams, both in-house and from other departments, whose guidance and contributions were invaluable throughout the journey. This achievement proves once again: engineering excellence isn’t just our goal- it’s our culture.


 


 






#TribePune's All Hands Meet: Real Conversations, Exciting Work, and a Look Ahead

We recently hosted an All Hands Meet— a great moment for all of us to come together to hear what’s happening across the business and connect as one team. 

Aditya Adavi, Center Head, BGSW Pune, kicked things off by sharing the current business landscape, where we’re headed, and how we’re doing against our goals. It set the tone for an open and informative session.

We also touched upon the FIT.Pune program, where our Field of Action (FoA) anchors and mentors gave a quick preview of the work happening across different focus areas. It was a great way for everyone to get a sense of the momentum building across the Pune team.

One of the most engaging parts of the session was the associate Q&A — honest questions, thoughtful answers, and a chance to have open conversations on what matters most to our teams.

We also had an Open Stage moment, where a few associates shared some of the unique and exciting projects they’ve been working on. It was inspiring to hear the stories behind the work and see the passion our teams bring every day.

We wrapped up with a sneak peek at a few innovative ideas we’ve been building behind the scenes. 

Stay tuned for more on the FIT.Pune updates.


 


 






#TribePune | BD Connect Event Highlights

The recent BD Connect event in Pune, featuring Nellissery Mathew (BD/IRA-OE) and Narasimhan S (BD/IRA-MDM), delivered critical updates and fostered engagement across the team. Matthew provided a comprehensive review of BD's business performance, setting the stage for the company's strategic objectives for the upcoming year. He emphasized the company's commitment to both groundbreaking innovation and streamlined, efficient execution. Building on this foundation, Narashiman offered invaluable insights into the advancements being made in Master Data Management (MDM), highlighting the advanced tools driving progress in this crucial area. A dynamic Q&A session provided a platform for associates to directly engage with Matthew and Narashiman, fostering open communication and addressing key questions. The Pune BD team further enriched the event by showcasing local operations, including strategic initiatives such as Syniti, SAP Academy training, and SAP BTP training programs. 

 Here's what the leaders say about their visit to BGSW Pune:

Nellissery Mathew (BD/IRA-OE)

"Many thanks for the warm welcome to the Pune center.

Pune has a strong talent pool, thanks to its proximity to major IT service providers and Automotive OEMs. The center offers a great blend of experienced professionals and young talent, creating an ideal environment for Bosch Digital growth at Pune. The close collaboration between the User Departments and IT teams helps to strengthen SAP S/4HANA Rollouts from Pune. 

I am truly impressed by the team’s energy and commitment - kudos to the BGSW Pune team!"

Narasimhan S (BD/IRA-MDM)

"My experience with the Pune team has been truly excellent. If I were to describe the team in one word, it would be ‘Unique.’ The sense of unity and the strong drive to contribute meaningfully to BD’s business objectives are clearly visible. I encourage the team to continue this momentum and actively take on key roles in S/4 rollout projects. I also invite you to share ideas on how we can further streamline stakeholder coordination and strengthen operations in our S/4 rollout programs. Let’s continue to collaborate towards the successful industrialization of rollouts. Wishing all of us all the very best." 

 Another highlight was the informal Coffee Connect session with Sudarshan Srinath (BD/SWD-BEA). He shared some personal stories that sparked a lot of fresh thinking about innovation. The relaxed atmosphere made it easy for everyone to chat openly, share ideas, and brainstorm together.


 


 






#TribePune | SX Talent Family’s Open House

On June 18th, the SX Talent Family in Pune hosted a dynamic Open House event, creating a valuable platform for associates to connect directly with senior leadership. Leaders - Talent Head Ulindala Bala Suresh Reddy (SX/ETF-MM SDS/BSV), Talent Director Badrinarayanan G R (SX/ETD-MM), along with Chaturvedi Abhishek (SX/ETD1-MM) and Mohandass Manoj (SX/ETD2-MM) joined the session, sharing their insights and addressing a wide range of thoughtful questions from the team. Their presence and open engagement made the event both informative and energizing.

Supporting the dialogue were Pune-based leaders Prakash Anil (BGSW/PJ-ESO3-PUN), Chintamani Neha (BGSW/HRL-BP-PUN), and Rajashree Subir Chakraborty (BGSW/PJ-ESO4-PUN), whose perspectives added local relevance and depth to the conversations. Their contributions helped foster a strong sense of connection and alignment within the Pune team.

A key highlight of the event was a recognition ceremony celebrating associates who have made outstanding contributions to critical projects. Certificates were presented by Bala and Anil, honoring excellence, ownership, and dedication across the team.

Kudos to

Sahu Yamini (SX/ETD11-MM), Sarode Mansi Rajendra (SX/ETD12-MM), Mohana Vamsi Batchu (SX/ETD12-MM), Singh Anamika Uday Pratap (SX/ETD2-MM), Chirmade Charulata Chandrakant (SX/ETD2-MM), Singhan Pranav (SX/ETD2-MM HC/BDO-S2), Kumar Shivam (SX/ETD2-MM, Kumar Shivam (SX/ETD2-MM), Shubham R Tehre (SX/ETD2-MM), Sharma Sneha (SX/ETD2-MM), Deshmukh Sanket Bhagwan (SX/ETD13-MM), Bhuma Venkata Naga Lalitha Sai Rohit (SX/ETD12-MM), Sinha Ritesh (SX/ETD2-MM), Dipti Raju Bansod (SX/ETD3-MM)

This Open House served as a strong reflection of our ongoing commitment to transparency, collaboration, and recognizing the impact of our people. Shoutout to everyone who participated and made the event a success.


 


 






#TribePune | SDS Talent Family’s Open House

Leaders - Talent Head Ulindala Bala Suresh Reddy (SX/ETF-MM SDS/BSV), Talent Directors, Badrinarayanan G R (SX/ETD-MM) and Balachandar Dhandapani (SDS/BSV-IF) along with Asif Mohiuddin Mohammed (SDS/BSV-ES4) and Arsh Gupta (BGSW/HRL-BP4) met the SDS Talent Family.

Joining from Pune, Prakash Anil (BGSW/PJ-ESO3-PUN) and Neha Chintamani (BGSW/HRL-BP-PUN) brought their unique insights and experience, adding depth to the conversations and creating a space for open dialogue.

One of the most heartening parts of the day was a dedicated session with our apprentices. Leaders shared their thoughts on Bosch’s culture, values, and what it means to grow within the organization. Their guidance was not just informative — it was genuinely uplifting, helping apprentices see the bigger picture of their journey.

The event ended on a celebratory note with honoring associates who have made significant contributions to key projects. Certificates were presented by leaders making the moment even more special. It was a proud reminder of the passion, commitment, and talent that drives SDS forward every day.

Kudos to:

Nair Saumya Sukumaran (SDS/BSV-ES4), Sarang Shinde (SDS/BSV-ES2), Sanket Sanjay Garbhe (SDS/BSV-ES2), Pankaj Kumar (SDS/BSV-ES2), Srijesh Ramchandran Nair (SDS/BSV-IF1), Nawale Shubham Babasaheb (SDS/BSV-ES3), Akshay Shah (SDS/BSV-ES3), Himanshu Deshmukh (SDS/BSV-ES3), Akash Bhausaheb Gadekar (SDS/BSV-ES3), Mayur Kulkarni (SDS/BSV-ES3), Ingole Praveen Gopal (SDS/BSV-IF2), Gupta Aman (SDS/BSV-IF2), Kumar Ajay (SDS/BSV-IF2)


 


 








#TribePune | The Culture Journey Continues…         

We hit the brakes to take a quick pulse check with our associates and see exactly where we stand in Pune’s culture-building journey. The survey results were truly impressive—and they confirmed we’re right on track.

To share these insights with our Culture Ambassadors and shape a focused action plan, we hosted a dedicated workshop.

Workshop Highlights:

*  Collaborated with our Culture Ambassadors to review and reflect on the Pune Culture Pulse Survey findings—celebrating strengths and identifying opportunities.

*  Defined the non-negotiable Bold, Boundaryless, Proud (BBP) values that will guide our behaviors and decisions.

*  Addressed key areas for improvement raised by associates, establishing clear next steps to drive lasting progress.

Throughout the session, Pune’s leadership team reflected on our journey since 2022 and reaffirmed their commitment to building a strong, values-led culture.

This movement is powered by voices from across our associate community—driving innovation, recognition, and learning. At Pune, the BBP journey is truly collaborative: every voice matters, and everyone makes a difference.

#TribePune | PROPEL 2025: Shaping Leadership at BGSW–Pune 

Continuing our commitment to cultivating leadership at BGSW–Pune, this year’s enhanced PROPEL Leadership Program launched with renewed energy—featuring 25 associates embarking on a transformative, experience-led journey.

The kickoff was initiated with opening remarks by Aditya Adavi (BGSW/ECH-PUN MS/KAM-EB SDS/SAM-SE), followed by inspiring messages from Prakash Anil (BGSW/PJ-ESO3-PUN), Kurade Dattatraya Ramchandra (BGSW/PJ-ESM-PUN), and Ramesh Palaniappan (BGSW/PJ-ESO1-PUN). Associates were introduced to peer coaches, mentors, and consultant—setting the stage for authentic connection and purpose-driven growth.

What makes PROPEL unique is its dual-track leadership development: participants engage in live business problem-solving, while peer coaches enhance their empathy and influence through hands-on coaching workshops.

The journey began with foundational sessions on Bosch Competence Model (BCM) and Design Thinking, equipping associates with creative and resilient approaches to leadership and innovation. This year, each strategic challenge has been carefully aligned with BGSW’s overarching goals—ensuring every project fuels both personal and organizational advancement.

As the 2025 cohort charts its path forward, they would be learning to lead and think business.


 


 








#TribePune | Summary of NE2-XC Visit          

Sanjeev Gondkar, Vice President MS/NE2-XC MS/EVC-XC, visited the Pune office for a focused team connect session in CW25. His engagements included a dynamic fireside chat with NE2-XC associates and focused discussions with individual sub-teams, supported by contextual facilitation from HRBP Bhardwaj Rohit. He offered valuable insights into key business strategies & highlighted the importance of strategic acquisitions and stressed on the concept of “China Speed”—a compelling approach to rapid execution critical for staying competitive in today’s fast-paced market. Throughout the discussions, he addressed the current business landscape, outlining actionable strategies for navigating challenges and embracing change. He emphasized the need for a growth mindset and encouraged associates to prepare for future ways of working

Team-level sessions anchored by Dedhia Nitin (MS/ECE-PN1-XC) (Passenger Vehicle & Talent Team) and Chandwadkar Amol Anant (MS/EVC-CV1-XC) (Commercial Vehicle) fostered open dialogue on aspirations, strengths, and development of NE-XC projects responsibilities growth at Center. These interactions enhanced collaboration and reinforced alignment with section and organizational goals

Sanjeev met with the Aditya Adavi, Pune Center Head and Core Team (anchored by Ramesh Palaniappan (BGSW/PJ-ESO1-PUN), for a strategic exchange on the NE-XC center’s roadmap. The discussion encompassed regional priorities such as IOEM, Systems Engineering, Business Acquisition representation, and Virtualization Engineering, along with innovation-driven strategies aimed at enhancing project efficiency—further reinforcing the center’s role in driving regional growth. The visit proved to be a valuable opportunity for associates to connect with Sanjeev, exchange ideas, and reaffirm their shared commitment to innovation and growth.

#TribePune | Chess Team Shines in Corporate Debut! 

The BGSW Pune Chess Team has made an impressive entry into the corporate chess scene — and what a debut it’s been!

From the very beginning, the team approached this with professionalism and passion. Our internal selection tournament was run like a true championship, complete with official boards, clocks, and a competitive spirit that set the tone.

Taking on some of the toughest competition — including seasoned players from clubs, our team held their ground and secured an outstanding 5th place finish. 

Meet the team behind the success:

*  Komarapuri Venkata Subhash (MS/EAI3-PS)

*  Rajendra Sunita Birnale (MS/ETD2-PS)

*  Satpute Sandeep (MS/ENB34-EM-PE)

*  Yadav Satyajeetsinh Sanjaysinh (MS/ETT4)

*  Gautam Balasubramaniam (MS/EAV4-PS)

This is more than just a great start — it's the beginning of something special for the BGSW Pune Chess Team. Onward and upward!

Subject: Income Tax Declaration - FY: 2025 - 2026
Body:
Dear Colleagues,

 

The Window period for associates to submit their income tax declarations for the Indian Financial Year April 2025 – March 2026 is now open.

 

Kindly ensure to go through attached documents “Income_Tax_Declaration_Notice” & “Simulation Tax Working between Old and New tax regimes”.  There are very important changes which are to be considered while simulating taxes between the Old and the New Tax regimes.

 

Important Points:

1.	Tax declaration Window period will be opened from 1st to 12th of every month till March 2026. 

IT Declarations - India <https://ph1.wdisp.bosch.com/sap/bc/webdynpro/sap/hress_itdl_ee_in?sap-wd-configId=HRESS_ITDL_AC_EE_IN> 

2.	Associates who have opted for the OLD TAX REGIME can declare and upload their income tax proofs in ESS. Associates who have opted for the NEW TAX REGIME need not declare and submit any tax proofs.
3.	Whenever there is any change in the status of the declarations submitted relating to HRA / Interest on Housing loan / other investments, the associates are obligated to revise their income tax declarations accordingly to reflect the correct status and comply with the Indian Income tax rules and regulations.

 

Particulars

Details

House Rent Allowance (HRA)  (only under old tax regime)

Associates have to declare the ACTUAL rental declarations along with necessary proofs through ESS.

HRA paid will be considered as taxable till the submission of the rental declaration with necessary proofs and tax exemption will be provided only from the month in which the tax declaration has been submitted / verified / approved.

Interest on Housing Loan (only under old tax regime)

Associates have to create request (along with necessary document i.e. Interest certificate from the bank, property ownership proof, notorized affidavit-wherever applicable) through ESS. 

Tax exemptions will be considered only after successful verification / validation of the declaration and the documents submitted

Sec 80C & Sec 80D deductions (only under old tax regime)

Associates have the option to submit their PROPOSED declarations (without submitting any proofs) till the month of November 2025. However, tax calculations will be done based only on actual investment proofs submitted under actual declarations thro ESS from the month of Dec 2025 till March 2026.

 

 

In case of any queries, request you to raise SSF ticket <https://inside.bosch.com/irj/portal?NavigationTarget=navurl%3A%2F%2F334c4e872d0993099e373657c8f8b8c8>
