Who is the target group?

 

The target group of the WBT Export Control and Sanctions has been redefined:

a.	All associates SL1+ or similar (except MED) and all associates with leadership responsibility, specifically with the role ‘Manager’ in the HR system HR Global /EC,
b.	All associates in accounting, Research & Development, Purchasing, Sales,
c.	All associates in manufacturing, Logistics, Quality Management, whose tasks surpass pure staff work, production or assembly, in particular team leaders and project managers,
d.	All Export Control Managers and Export Control Local Contact Persons,
e.	All associates within C/TX, C/LS, C/CM, C/AU, BD/RMO,
f.	All associates with external business contacts and corresponding decision-making authority existing or potential external customers, cooperation partners, distributors, suppliers, freight forwarders, consultants, service providers, banks and insurance companies,
g.	In doubt: Participation is mandatory

 	
 

 	
 

 	
 

 	


What do I have to do as an associate?

 

As associate to whom a Compliance training measure has been assigned, you will be responsible for completing the training on time (see RBGF 120, attachment <https://rb-wam.bosch.com/socos-rb/SOCOS/documents/ccm99/rbgf/10070/RBGF-00120-002_ANH_N_EN_2025-10-01.pdf>  2, 4.1.6 <https://rb-wam.bosch.com/socos-rb/SOCOS/documents/ccm99/rbgf/10070/RBGF-00120-002_ANH_N_EN_2025-10-01.pdf> )

 

 

 



What do I have to do as a supervisor?

            

As a supervisor with target responsibility, you will identify the associates to be trained according to the respective target group definition, make assignments in the HR Global training IT system, and ensure the timely completion of the training (see RBGF 120, attachment 2, 4.1.5.1 <https://rb-wam.bosch.com/socos-rb/SOCOS/documents/ccm99/rbgf/10070/RBGF-00120-002_ANH_N_EN_2025-10-01.pdf> )

 

 	
 

 	
 

 	


The curriculum will be automatically assigned to the following target groups: a), b), e). Manual assignments by the responsible supervisors must be made within one month for c), d), f), g) and all associates must complete by January 31, 2026

Subject: The Weekly Wrap 26th September 2025
Body:
26th September 2025


 






Infineon Tech Day 2025 @ BGSW 

The Infineon Tech Day, hosted by NE-PG MS/EEH Dept., highlighted innovations in automotive MCUs. Infineon showcased next-generation products incl. TC4xx, Traveo™, PSOC™ and the upgraded TC3xx@400MHz, along with presentations on latest technologies including RRAM, NVM, RISC-V based RC1 etc. 

Event Highlights:

*      Panel Discussion – “How do Infineon and Bosch shape the future of the automotive industry?”

*      Traveo™ T2G & T2G Extension

*      PSOC™ BMS for Automotive Portfolio

*      AURIX™ TC4x Automotive MCUs

*      AURIX™ TC3xx Extension @ 400MHz

*      Latest Memory Technologies

*	RRAM
*	SEMPER™ X LPDDR Flash

*      AURIX™ RC1 - RISC-V Platform Architecture.

 

Demos Highlights:

*      I/O Aggregator Demo with TRAVEO T2G for SW-Centralized Automotive Ethernet Architectures

*      Light electrical vehicle LEV-X-in-1 Demo

*      AURIXTM Security demo “phase 2” (TC4x vs.TC3x)

*      TRAVEOTM T2G Cluster MTBTM GFX support with QT (software driven)

*      RISC-V prototype

*      PSOC™ steering wheel with multi-zonal Hands-on-Detection  & heating function

*      TRAVEO™ T2G Connected Cluster with map mirroring : PSOC™ Multitouch: Gen7L + TRAVEO-T2G

*      HV-BMS : Synchronized V/I sensing and EIS demo: AURIX™ TC3 + PSOC™ 4 HVPA-SPM + TLE9018

*      SEMPER™ AUTOSAR FLS Demo (TC4x, SEMPER™)

This event showcased multiple product portfolios with comprehensive roadmap to accommodate dynamic market demands.

For more information refer our Docupedia <https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence2/display/MSEEH/IFX+Tech+Day+2025>  page.


 


 





CFW Day @ BGSW

CFW Day was hosted @ BGSW - ADU campus to emphasize on how it can enable SW development to be on the top position for mobility SW & service solutions by

*	Harmonizing architectures, processes, methods and tools across BBM
*	Making them ready for future ways of development in changing automotive ecosystems

The day started with Keynote from Alexander Springer (M/PJ-CFW), Damian Dyrbusch (MS/NE-XC) & Santosh P (MS/ETH-PG, MS/ECF).

Alex provided quick view on Vision & Transformation needed in current BBM context & strategy. Detailed out CFW operation model.

Damian extended with his journey in CFW & how he sees SW development at XC can gain speed, efficiency & resilience.

Santosh further gave insights on HOW part which includes Configurator, SaaS environment & Warehouse as pillars of CFW.

Click here <https://connect.bosch.com/communities/service/html/communityview?communityUuid=d8fd5fc6-958a-4e55-9483-72a8bb409841#fullpageWidgetId=We44bd2dca0b5_4306_86c6_ec6f3b6f9409&file=3562bc77-8836-42b5-8037-f3671655b987>  to know more.


 


 






BD/WPA-CSS Innovation Day 2025: Driving Ideas, Empowering Teams, Building the Future Together

🎥 Have a look at our event video: Link <https://bosch.mediaspace.de.kaltura.com/media/BDWPA-CSS%20Innovation%20Day%202025/0_3am42al9> 

BD/WPA-CSS Tribe hosted its first Innovation Day under the Accord Initiative on 09th September 2025 at BGSW, bringing together diverse teams, industry leaders, and collaborators to showcase creativity, research, and practical solutions for real-world challenges in digital transformation.

The event opened with inspiring addresses from Mr. Dhamotharan Velumani (BD/DIA-GTC4 Chapter Lead) and Mr. Rajesh E S (Tribe Lead). The highlight of the event was keynote session from Mr. Nasam Srinivasalu, Senior Technical Director, Bosch Mobility, who shared thought-provoking perspectives on the transformative role of Generative AI.

The event featured engaging presentations and live demonstrations of the top 5 Proofs of Concept (POCs) and Ideation Papers, showcasing groundbreaking solutions. The demonstration energized the room, captivating the audience and earning enthusiastic appreciation. Throughout the day, an engaging and interactive exchange of ideas unfolded, fostering lively discussions and knowledge sharing among participants. Each innovation was thoughtfully evaluated based on creativity, scalability, and its relevance to pressing industry challenges, ensuring a comprehensive and impactful showcase.

The presence of Ms. Sujatha D, Regional President for BD India and Alliance Lead for S4Hana rollout, as Guest of Honor further elevated the occasion. Outstanding contributions and participation were recognized through awards and felicitations, with engaging activities—including a quiz contest and a surprise recognition for the Best Interactive Participant—ensuring a high-energy conclusion.

Key takeaways from the day highlighted the importance of an efficiency-driven mindset, a customer-first approach and AI-first, and the recognition that innovation is a continuous journey. Selected solutions will advance into pilot implementations, while other ideations will inform future projects, reinforcing our commitment to a culture where collaboration and innovation drive long-term success.

At BD/WPA-CSS Tribe, Innovation Day 2025 is only the beginning—we look forward to building on this momentum and shaping the future together.

EMH’s Synovate – BGSW Bangalore

The MS/EMH team hosted a successful marketplace event at BGSW Bangalore headed by Sudhir Vijay Sattigeri, highlighting the Design for Environment (DFE) & Sustainability (LCA & Eco-design), Benchmarking, Costing, Competitor innovation Study, CAD digitalization, Connector design topics. Attended by nearly 110+ delegates and opened by Section Head Mr. Srikanth Hegde, the event showcased MS/EMH department capabilities by displaying their projects and related case study presentations.

Highlighted Topics and Product displays:

*	DFE: Accelerator pedal module, Injector, Nozzle holder Assembly, iTRAMS
*	Sustainability: Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) & Eco design (New Services) 
*	Benchmarking & Costing: Radar, Silverbox, e-Axle, Charcon, ABS, Pump, Governor, BSH Products, Tool Costing, Case studies & Success stories
*	CAD Digitalization: 3D Modeling and Design support in All CAD Software, CAD Migration, Reverse Engineering and Remastering support, PLM/PDM Integration Support, 3D PMI (Model Based Definition) Support
*	Connector & wiring harness: Testing & wiring harness, Design and Development, Series Support, COC.

 

Stakeholder’s View:

*	Skynovate: Our department work helps innovation to reach the sky
*	EMH’s Diversity from engineering and product cost analysis to digitalization and sustainability helps us approach challenges from multiple angles.
*	An all-in-one solution combining cost engineering and sustainability for optimized budget and environmental impact.


 


 






Agile Outcomes Day 2025: Business Outcomes from ATO's Development Program

ATO hosted the Agile Outcomes Day on 16th Sep, an engaging and insightful event that brought together all participants of our Agile development programs conducted till date.  The event witnessed enthusiastic participation from all batches, with participants sharing their journeys and reflections, sparking meaningful conversations on the real-world impact of Agile practices.”

The event started with an invocation by Navneet Pandey followed by an overview of the development programs from ATO by Sandeep which highlighted the outcomes and feedback from all the 6 programs that were conducted last year.  Sandhya from ALDP@EVC <mailto:ALDP@EVC>  batch highlighted the problem-solving approach using 5Why and HMW technique which improved the predictability of sprints.  Huy from ALDP@BGSV <mailto:ALDP@BGSV>  batch explained how agile mindset was employed in the infrastructure optimization which resulted in 23K euros savings per month.  Adithya from ALDP@ESD <mailto:ALDP@ESD>  batch emphasized the need to not fall for symptoms but to ensure the root of the problem is sovled to keep long term customer relations.  Jyotsna from AMDP@BLR <mailto:AMDP@BLR>  batch looked into the data from team assessments which helped her to get good insights in improving the team performance in achieving over 80% predictability.  Darshan from PODP@BLR <mailto:PODP@BLR>  batch talked on how the course helped him in his role of a PO to develop the CS platform and designing the logo.  

The highlight of the program was the guest talk from Dr. Kaushik Hatti, where he talked on the importance of CS, usage of AI for personalized coaching of team members, various methods employed by their team to increase the effectiveness of their team resulting in quick release of their product and increased employee engagement...

A Huge Thanks to all our Agile Champions who presented and to all colleagues who participated to make the event successful!

A special thanks to those who actively contributed to the success of these programs and continue to drive the Agile movement forward; Dinesh Roy L (BGSW/ETT BGSW/PJ-ETT-ETB) for supporting all Agile initiatives at T-Hub, Udupa Parameshwara E G BGSW/QMM-PM BGSW/QMM-PM-MAT) and Subbaramu G (BGSW/QMM-PM, MS/QMM) for championing Agile culture with a focus on business outcomes. 

The event was not only a celebration of learning but also a testament to the power of collaboration and continuous improvement—the very essence of Agile. Agile outcomes Day 2025 left us all motivated to embrace change, foster teamwork, and drive innovation in everything we do..

Want to Be Part of the Agile Revolution?

For more details on Agile Development Programs, reach out to ATO Lead, Sandeep Hublikar (sandeep.hublikar@in.bosch.com <mailto:sandeep.hublikar@in.bosch.com> ).

Agility is more than Process, Methods and Tools, it’s a mindset to create business outcomes. And with programs like ALDP, AMDP, PODP, Growth Mindset Bosch is ensuring that leaders of today are ready for the challenges of tomorrow.

Customer Visit : Suzuki Motor Corporation (SMC) and Maruti Suzuki India Limited (MSIL) Customers at Bosch 

On September 19th, 2025, Bosch had the pleasure of hosting Mr. Yamada Shinji (SMC) – Head of Powertrain Calibration, Mr. Tamai Nobutaka (SMC) – Head of Advanced Projects, Mr. Vikram Khanna (MSIL) – Head of Powertrain Calibration, Mr. Kinome Yasuhiro (MSIL) – Head of Powertrain Calibration, and Mr. Hemant Mehra (MSIL) – Project Management , for a collaborative visit. The purpose of this visit was to review ongoing projects, assess quality standards, and strategize for upcoming projects. Held at Bosch Bengaluru (Adugodi), the event provided both teams with a valuable opportunity to engage in productive discussions and further strengthen the partnership.

Mr. Kumar R Anjan (PS/RP-IN PS/CA-IN), Regional President PS India ; Mr. Sathyananda Sharma L B (MS/PJ-ECU-IN, PS-SC/RBU-IN), Regional Business Unit Electronic Controls India; Mr. K U Ravindra (PS/NE-IN PS-CV/ENG-IN), Vice President Engineering India Diesel ; Mr. Prashant Satkhed (IN/SO1 M/PJ-MAV SU/SOE-IN) , Vice President Original Equipment Sales India;  Mr. Battur Santosh (MS/ECS-PS PS-SC/PAB-SH-IN) , Service House India Responsibilities;  shared their valuable insights and guidance during the workshop. This event brought together key partners from Bosch India and Japan, with participation from leaders across various Bosch departments, including Mr. Fuji Yoshihiko, General Manager (PS-SC/ECG-JP); Ms. Shruthi Noel Kueri, Program Director (EPJ-PS); Mr. Yamamoto Kousuke (PS/CTO PS/STO1), GCT Sales SMC/MSIL, Mr. Hitoshi Okuyama, (PS/CSU PS/ETO) General Manager Sales ; Mr. Singh Amandeep (PS/CSU-IN), Customer Team Maruti Suzuki Sales India. The active involvement of middle management leaders further enriched the discussions with diverse perspectives throughout the workshop.

During the visit, SMC/MSIL customers expressed their appreciation for the Bosch team’s transparency and preparedness. They provided positive feedback on the ECU (software, hardware, and calibration) development process, along with constructive suggestions for further enhancement. SMC & MSIL presented their future business strategy, key vehicle programs and their expectations from Bosch. Key topics covered during the discussions included project timelines, quality assurance strategies, and opportunities for future collaboration. Both teams aligned on actionable steps to address the feedback received and committed to maintaining regular communication going forward. The visit concluded on a positive note, with representatives from SMC and MSIL expressing confidence in Bosch’s capabilities and dedication to excellence. The event underscored the importance of open dialogue and collaborative teamwork in driving shared success.

👏 Overall, it was a memorable afternoon that highlighted the power of community, mentorship, and self-empowerment, reinforcing She Rise’s vision to uplift and inspire.

#TribePune | Strategic Engagement with ARAI (Automotive Electronic CoC) – Advancing Battery Circularity for India

The BGSW-Pune Re.OS team recently visited ARAI’s Homologation and Automotive Electronics divisions in Chakan, engaging with senior leadership including Deputy Director Abhijit B. Mulay, Dr. Ravindra Kumar, and Sreekumar U. We showcased our Digital Battery Circularity Platform (Re-OS) and held forward-looking discussions on how India’s emerging Battery Adhaar Passport framework would be strongly connected with this Platform too.

ARAI expressed strong interest in our collaborative approach and welcomed Bosch’s inclusion in their technical committee shaping future battery ID parameter proposals. This marks a significant step in aligning Bosch’s domain expertise with national policy efforts in their foreseeable committee formation with few industry leaders.

We’re now planning deeper engagement through lab visits and pilot demonstrations, translating ARAI’s policy vision into tangible use cases. This initiative positions BGSW as a key enabler in India’s battery ecosystem-driving innovation, standardization, and new business opportunities in the Battery Circularity with electrification and sustainability drives.

BGSW-Pune was represented by Salil Inamdar (BGSW/EII C/IDR-IN), Tewari Kanishk (BGSW/PJ-ESO-PUN), and Ramesh Palaniappan (BGSW/PJ-ESO1-PUN).

Body:
10th October 2025


 





Guidelines for External Interactions and Social Media at BGW         

As Bosch associates, we are ambassadors of the brand, and our collective voices shape BGSW’s brand presence. Whether engaging with media, speaking at events, or interacting on social media, we must remember to communicate responsibly and align with organizational values.

Please familiarize yourself and adhere to the below established guidelines at BGSW for any external interactions and social media engagements :

Guidelines for all External Interactions with Media Houses, Event Engagements <https://connect.bosch.com/communities/service/html/communityview?communityUuid=d8fd5fc6-958a-4e55-9483-72a8bb409841#fullpageWidgetId=We44bd2dca0b5_4306_86c6_ec6f3b6f9409&file=f6e6c3a4-87e0-4e64-a4a1-2f2f46b02347> 

Social Media Guidelines at BGSW <https://connect.bosch.com/communities/service/html/communityview?communityUuid=d8fd5fc6-958a-4e55-9483-72a8bb409841#fullpageWidgetId=We44bd2dca0b5_4306_86c6_ec6f3b6f9409&file=c024521c-c85d-4808-8c33-8c76ebbd70b8> 


 


 






BGSW Multimarket Customer Engagements

Mr. Fantini Alessandro (NE Compact Hydraulics Business) and Mr. De Luca Antonio, Product Head for HIC (Hydraulic Integrated Circuits) and CMC (Compact Motion Control), visited BGSW Multimarket. During the visit, they engaged with the Multimarket Product Engineering team and participated in deep-dive sessions covering topics such as casting design, FMEA at DC-CH, and hardware capabilities aligned with DC Business Units. The visit also included a plant tour of Indo Shell Cast. BGSW showcased its digital, AI, and GenAI capabilities leading to detailed discussions on potential applications particularly in areas like cost calculation based on the design proposal, trace and early root cause analysis leveraging AI.


 


 





BGSW Multimarket at Industry Roundatable on “Responsible AI in the Agentic Era         

Mr. Harish Babu Musarakallu (Tech Expert, Home Comfort) and Mr. Pavan M Laxmeshwar (Department Head, AI Practice) from BGSW Multimarket participated at the NASSCOM Agentic AI Confluence 2025, the Industry Roundtable on Responsible AI in the Agentic Era convened leading experts and practitioners to discuss how India can pioneer safe, ethical, and accountable AI systems in this new frontier as a precursor to India AI Summit.

The discussion unpacked the transformative potential and rising risks of Agentic AI — where intelligent agents act with minimal supervision, amplifying both innovation and impact.

Harish and Pavan brought in unique perspectives on how BGSW is adopting Agentic AI enabling safety and trust balancing innovation with accountability.

They further reinforced continued commitment from BGSW in shaping India's Responsible Agentic AI ecosystem.


 


 






BGSW Multimarket at Panel discussion 𝐨𝐧 “Agentic AI Adoption in Manufacturing”

The NASSCOM Agentic AI Confluence 2025 served as a premier industry platform showcasing the rapid evolution of Agentic and Generative AI — from intelligent automation to autonomous, goal-driven ecosystems transforming enterprises. Leaders across technology, academia, and industry deliberated on AI governance, multi-agent architectures, real-world implementations, and responsible scaling.

Lakshmi Sunanda T (Program Director, Home comfort) had the privilege to represent BGSW in the Business Track Panel on “Self-Healing Factory: Generative AI in Motion.” The session spotlighted how Generative and Agentic AI are redefining manufacturing resilience through autonomous diagnostics, adaptive process optimization, and self-correcting systems. The discussion underscored the shift from predictive to proactive and self-healing operations, enabling improved uptime, productivity, and decision intelligence on the shop floor.

Our keynote emphasized the fusion of domain engineering with intelligent agents, showcasing how GenAI can be seamlessly embedded into industrial ecosystems to achieve higher efficiency, sustainability, and scalability — marking a key step toward the intelligent factory of the future. We also shared examples of our Agentic AI frameworks for manufacturing, including Maintenance co-pilots, Talk to Data agents, that enable contextual insights and autonomous decision support across factory operations. As part of our broader strategy, we are continuously adapting and scaling our capabilities to stay ahead of the evolving Agentic AI landscape, driving innovation and transformation across the industrial value chain.


 


 








Bosch SDS Showcases Future-Proof IoT Management at The Things Conference 2025         

At The Things Conference 2025 in Amsterdam, Bosch SDS demonstrated the power of the Bosch IoT Remote Manager, showcasing how millions of connected devices can be managed securely, reliably, and at scale. Live demos featured multi-protocol support, flexible OTA updates, and seamless LoRaWAN integration—addressing key market demands for future-proof IoT solutions.

Kai Hackbart, Head of Products and Solutions Europe, delivered an inspiring keynote, “Future-Proof by Design: Building IoT Solutions that Endure,” and led a panel discussion, “From Data to Decisions: How IoT and Agentic AI Are Transforming Industry.” He also highlighted how IoT, Generative AI, and emerging Agentic AI are driving the next wave of intelligent and autonomous systems.

The Bosch SDS booth attracted strong engagement and customer interest, resulting in numerous high-value discussions that continue beyond the event.

GS Global Award 2025: Honoring excellence across the globe  

In a time of global economic challenges and headwind, motivating teams and acknowledging outstanding contributions remains a priority. Recently, Global Business Services hosted the GS Global Award established to shine a spotlight on this excellence. The award provides a global stage for recognition, celebrates collective successes, and fosters the motivation that fuels progress. At its core, the award is a vital contributor to the strategic framework of GS. By showcasing groundbreaking work, the GS Global Award strengthens the employer brand, instills a deep sense of pride throughout the GS team, and powerfully reinforces the WIN mentality that is crucial for success. It has been a successful awards round for India, with GS India recognized for outstanding participation in the Global Award through high submission and voting rates. In addition to winning the regional Continuous Improvement Process (CIP) Award where two projects from India were honored for their exceptional improvement initiatives, India also secured the Collaboration Award for one of its projects. By recognizing the very best of GS, past achievements are not just celebrated – the innovations that will define success for years to come are inspired. To know more, click here <https://bzo.bosch.com/bzo/en/article_page_648962.html> !


 


 








Apple Connect | Bosch x Apple Automotive Collaboration         

Engineering Tomorrow’s Mobility. Together.

Bosch Global Software Technologies (BGSW), through MS/ECO (NEO ESI ART), is driving innovation in automotive connectivity and infotainment with over a decade of expertise, 100+ certifications, and partnerships with 10+ global OEMs. Our strengths span Smartphone Integration (Apple CarPlay, Android Auto), Connectivity (Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, USB), and Media Services (Google Automotive Services), supported by leadership in certifications like CarPlay, Android Auto, and MFi.

On Sept 9, 2025, BGSW was invited to Apple’s Bangalore office for a strategic workshop with Apple’s Automotive Programs team. Discussions focused on Next-Gen CarPlay Ultra, 2-Wheeler CarPlay for India, and Bosch’s proposal to co-develop certification standards. Both teams tackled certification challenges - fragmented pipelines, manual testing, and tooling gaps - while Bosch showcased its DevOps-driven automation via FACETs 3 cloud platform.

This collaboration strengthens a shared vision: lean certification, tooling excellence, and accelerated innovation for next-gen mobility experiences.

Click here <https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/display/xccpneoperations/Apple_Bosch_Connect_2025>  to read more. 

To know more about NEO ESI ART, click here <https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=4801053460&src=contextnavpagetreemode> .

Engineers Day at EEM-PS  

September 15th 2025, a day dedicated to honoring the visionary spirit of engineers, was celebrated with immense enthusiasm and intellectual fervor at EEM-PS (@ Cob & Kor locations)

It was a vibrant tapestry of insightful tech talks, engaging informative sessions and celebration of inventions, all centered around “Passion for Engineering and the pride of being an Engineer”

The Tech talks gave insights on BOSCH innovation framework & few inventions where ideas turned into earnings for BOSCH. It was fascinating to know that few patents are already into products in market. Wide scope of ideas was demonstrated from Automotive segment to Daily appliances, which gave the big picture on different areas to explore and innovate, perfectly adhering to “Invented for Life”

As a cherry on top, EEM-PS Innovation Contributors who filed 5 patents & published 4 papers were honored which was a great inspiration to the aspiring inventors. The energy throughout the event was palpable. It was a powerful reminder of the collective impact engineers have on every facet of our lives – from the infrastructure we use daily to the groundbreaking technologies that promise a brighter tomorrow.

We extend our heartfelt gratitude to all our speakers for their invaluable contributions and to everyone who joined us in making this Engineers Day celebration a resounding success. Let's continue to champion innovation, embrace challenges, and engineer a better future, together.


 


 






A Wild Day Out – BD/PA-TOA COB Outing 2025!

Our much-awaited annual team outing took place on 25th September 2025 at SR Jungle Resort, Anaikatti, bringing together over 90 enthusiastic participants for a day filled with fun, bonding, and unforgettable memories. The journey itself set the tone with music, dance, and high energy. On arrival, the day began on a good note with a welcome drink, speeches, and a cake-cutting ceremony, followed by a series of engaging team games and activities that sparked laughter and teamwork. A lively mimicry performance, DJ music, and spontaneous dance sessions kept the excitement going, while a delicious lunch and evening tea added to the experience. Thanks to the management for all the support. The event concluded with a vibrant group dance, leaving everyone refreshed, reconnected, and recharged for the journey ahead. Amidst our busy schedules and daily tasks, this outing offered a refreshing break — a perfect pause to recharge and reconnect beyond work


 


 





Winning With Women Hosts the Second Edition of Women Summit 2025 in Coimbatore          

On 26th September 2025, Winning With Women, the ARG of DEI, successfully hosted the second edition of Women Summit 2025 in Coimbatore, with live streaming connecting multiple locations. The summit’s inspiring theme, “Leading Transformation with Impact,” set the tone for a day full of empowerment and insight.

The event was honored by the presence of our esteemed leaders, including Padmaja A R, Executive Vice President and Member of the Executive Leadership; Dattatri Salagame, Managing Director; Naved Narayan, Vice President Mobility Solutions and Cob Center Head; Guru Mallikarjuna, Senior Vice President, Mobility Solutions; and Padma Neela J, DEI Head.

The summit focused on three powerful themes throughout the sessions:

Say It – Encouraging the courage to voice ideas, share personal stories, and inspire change.

Own It – Emphasizing executive presence, confidence, and accountability.

Change It – Championing transformation, breaking barriers, and fostering inclusive pathways.

Participants experienced a rich blend of leadership insights, engaging stories, interactive product pitches, and inspiring talks delivered by senior leaders, entrepreneurs, and DEI champions. The day culminated with a powerful star talk and a gratitude gala, leaving attendees motivated and ready to lead with impact.

For those who missed the live event, the full summit is available for offline viewing on Bosch Tube. <https://bosch.mediaspace.de.kaltura.com/media/WWW%20Summit%202025%20-%20Leading%20Transformation%20with%20Impact%20-%20Say%20It%20!%20Own%20It%20!%20Change%20It%20!/0_erldeis9> 


 


 






#TribePune Lean-Agile Dojo – Leaders & Practitioners Training

To strengthen BGSW’s Value Stream culture, the Lean-Agile Dojo—an immersive, classroom-based training program for Leaders and Practitioners was launched at Pune in association with T-Hub.

As agility is essential for delivering value at speed, this initiative equips teams to lead change, collaborate effectively, and apply Lean-Agile principles in real-world scenarios

The program was facilitated by Anand Murthy Raj, a Global Lean-Agile Coach with over 25 years of experience, who led the sessions with deep insights and practical frameworks. 

Program Snapshot

*  The Lean Agile Practitioners Dojo conducted for Level 52 & 53 focused on execution excellence: Lean-Agile principles, team development, problem-solving, and sustaining change.

*  The Lean Agile Leaders Dojo conducted for Level 54 and above focused on building strategic agility: Lean-Agile mindset, VSO model, Value Stream Mapping, and Agile Framework 4.0.


 


 





#TribePune | Summary of Datta's Visit and Strategic Discussions

During Datta's recent visit to Pune, key discussions centered around Field of Actions (FoAs) under the Fit.Pune strategic topics, with a specific focus on actions planned for the upcoming quarter and alignment with FoA anchors.

At Pune’s “Lunch with Datta,” conversations spanned from the current market context and its organizational impact to our collective path toward Strategy & Vision 2030.


 


 






#TribePune | ARAI Training – Automotive Safety & Homologation

The first batch of EOS Pune associates successfully completed the 2-day domain training program on "Automotive Safety & Homologation", conducted by ARAI. 

The training covered a wide range of topics including road safety requirements, the safety roadmap, an overview of the Indian automotive industry, automotive regulations, and the homologation process. It also included sessions on active and passive safety systems, AIS 145 standards, sensors and actuators in safety applications, and the Bharat NCAP framework.

A major highlight of the program was the Passive Safety Lab visit on the second day, where the ARAI team provided detailed insights into vehicle crash testing procedures. Various crash scenarios such as frontal, side, and rear impacts were explained, along with the types of crash test dummies used to simulate human responses during collisions. These dummies are equipped with advanced instrumentation to measure acceleration, forces, and impact data. This data helps engineers understand injury risks and develop safety features like airbags and seatbelts, ultimately improving vehicle crashworthiness and occupant protection.

The training emphasized how dummies are used across different crash tests to replicate the forces a human body would experience, enabling precise analysis of injury mechanisms. The session also covered the broader implications of crash testing and instrumentation, including injury prevention, enhanced vehicle safety, standardization across regulations, support for research and development, and inclusive design considerations for diverse occupant profiles.

The program gave associates a real feel for the day-to-day work in the passive safety domain and deepened their understanding of the importance of crash testing, homologation, and AIS standards. It was a well-received and impactful learning experience that strengthened domain knowledge and regulatory awareness.

Special thanks to T-Hub Dinesh Roy L (BGSW/ETT BGSW/PJ-ETT-ETB) and the entire T-Hub team for their support and enablement of this training. Appreciation is also extended to Raghu Narayana (MS/EOB2), Jadhav Pandurang (MS/PJ-SSL-OS-VM), Basavaraj Shivashankar Garadi (BGSW/PJ-ETT1), Vaidyaraman V V (BGSW/PJ-ETT4), Sandhana Mohan P (BGSW/PJ-ETT2 BGSW/PJ-ETT3), and Nitha Bhuvanen (MS/EOB2-VM) for their special curation of the program. Acknowledgment also goes to Karthik Rajapaul (BGSW/PJ-ETA-FTP) for coordinating and supporting the initiative. The support from OSS leadership Sunku Sreekanth (MS/EOB-VM MS/PJ-SWP-OS-VM) and BU Anchor, Ramesh Palaniappan (BGSW/PJ-ESO1-PUN) was commendable and instrumental in making this program a success.

Associate Reflections 

The training was highly effective and relevant for all participants, offering valuable insights into automotive safety and validation processes. Rajakumar E D (MS/PJ-SSL-OS-VM) highlighted the importance of understanding the Homologation and Type Approval process, Bharat NCAP and Star Ratings, and various AIS Standards, noting that the Passive Safety Laboratory visit was particularly impactful. Dhage Nilakantheshwar (MS/EOB12-VM) appreciated the training and found the LAB visit especially beneficial, gaining a clear understanding of the LAB instruments used in safety validation. Manasi Mahesh Naik (MS/EOB2) rated the experience a 10/10, emphasizing her learning around safety-critical topics such as frontal and side crashes, and how post-crash data is collected and analyzed. She also understood how crash dummies record biomechanical data—including forces, acceleration, and impact—to simulate human responses and guide improvements in vehicle safety systems.


 


 






#TribePune | Highlights from the ECS-PS Leadership Visit

The ECS-PS leadership team, including Section Heads, Heads of Engineering (HoEs), and Group Managers (GrMs), visited BGSW Pune. During the visit, multiple events were hosted, including a Town Hall, an associates connect session, and an "Ignite the Spark" session on leadership development, culminating in an eagerly awaited ECS-PS Pune team outing.

Santosh Battur, Service House Head & Section Head for ECS-PS, provided business updates for the Service House worldwide and within India, highlighting its focus areas, current status, and target position for 2030. He also presented the "We Change PS" initiatives and Focus Growth Zones for the Indian operations, emphasizing speed, agility, and ownership to maintain a leading position.

Gopala Krishna M R (MS/PJ-ECS-PS-PP) and Henzler Markus (MS/ECA-PS) provided updates on the ECS-PS performance program, developments in Cross-BU collaboration, and International Development Network (IDN) initiatives. Ashis Kumar Nayak (MS/EPA-PS), Sudhindra C V (MS/EAV-PS), and Deepak Shanbhag (MS/EAI-PS) presented an Indian OEM business update, outlining achievements, the future roadmap (including emission norms updates), and opportunities for Service House business growth.

AI-First: Girish K (MS/EAV3-PS) and Prabhu Dileep (MS/EPA-PS-EP) elaborated on the AI initiative rollout within ECS-PS, outlining key opportunities and potential business prospects driven by AI technologies.

Nithin Nath (MS/ECP-PJ3-PS) presented Connected Services business updates. 

Experience sharing by Chaudhari Kuldeepak Arun (MS/EAV1-PS), Salunkhe Mangesh Ramesh (MS/EAI2-PS), and Laxmikant Madhavrao Kushare (MS/EAI3-PS) about their cycling expedition from Pune to Pandharpur (approximately 250 km) emphasized the importance of wellness and physical fitness.

The Town Hall concluded with the felicitation of SH-IN Pitch winners, followed by recognition for service milestones, SAE paper contributions, patents, and project achievements, including sports events.

Ignite the Spark – Inspiring Leadership and Growth

An engaging "Ignite the Spark" session was a key highlight, featuring Jaladhi Thakkar, General Manager, HR, TATA Motors.  Thakkar delivered powerful insights on professional growth and the leadership journey, underscoring the "three E's"—Education, Experience, and Exposure—as essential for continuous development. His talk inspired a renewed sense of ownership among attendees.

To celebrate recent successes and achievements, the ECS-PS Pune team also enjoyed a memorable outing. With around 110 associates participating, this refreshing event fostered stronger collaboration and deeper bonds outside the office, leaving everyone re-energized and uplifted.

The event was successfully hosted by the highly motivated associates: Kukadolkar Kruti Manohar (MS/PJ-ECS-PS), Laxmikant Madhavrao Kushare (MS/EAI3-PS), Prahlad M (MS/EAV1-PS), Keerthana Karthikeyan (MS/EPA-PJ2-PS), Salunkhe Mangesh Ramesh (MS/EAI2-PS), Amol Deepak Badodkar (MS/EAI-PJ1-PS), Jangam Swapnil Vasant (MS/EPA-PJ2-PS), and Onkar Kumbhar (MS/EPA-PJ2-PS).


 


 








World Mental Health Day at BGSW Hyderabad         

On the occasion of World Mental Health Day BGSW Hyderabad came together to celebrate the importance of mental well-being with the theme — “Dialogue Across the Ages: Mental Health Through Generational Lenses.”

The session featured:
Mindfulness Moment – A guided practice to help associates center themselves and connect with the day’s theme.
Panel Discussion – Thought-provoking conversations across generations highlighting evolving perspectives on mental health.
Expert Talk – Insights from Ms. Raga Lahari, our in-house psychologist, on nurturing mental resilience and emotional balance.
Orientation – An overview of BGSW’s mental well-being programs and communities fostering continuous support.

The event was a meaningful reminder that together, we can build a stronger, more empathetic workplace culture. 

Connect. Cheer. Celebrate. – BGSW #ManaHyderabad  

On 25th September, associates at BGSW Hyderabad came together to celebrate Robert Bosch’s Birthday, honoring his vision of innovation, togetherness, and camaraderie. The event also marked the spirit of the festive season, blending fun, culture, and celebration in true #ManaHyderabad style.

The evening was filled with exciting activities — from a lively Open Mic where associates showcased their talents, to Fun Games and Quizzes that brought out everyone’s competitive spirit. The crowd cheered during the Mr. & Ms. Ethnic contest, celebrating vibrant traditional attire, and the day concluded with an energetic Dandiya Evening, spreading joy and festive vibes across the floor.

The celebration ended on a delightful note with snacks and conversations, creating moments of connection and shared happiness.

It was truly an evening that reflected the Bosch spirit — celebrating innovation, community, and culture, while cherishing the legacy of Robert Bosch.


 


 





Cricket Carnival 2025: A Day of Thrills and Team Spirit

The Cricket Carnival 2025 of SDS/ENG & SDS/BSV-ENG, held on 27th September, was a day filled with cricket, energy, and excitement. From the first ball in the morning to the last cheer in the evening, the matches kept everyone engaged and showcased the best of team spirit and sportsmanship.

 All five teams – Blazing Bullets, Mighty Spartans, Fearless Falcons, Digital Dynamos, and Thunder Strikers – put on thrilling performances, making every match a treat to watch. Subject: Don't Miss Out: Cybersecurity Around The World - 11th and 12th November 2025
Body:
Dear colleagues,

 

Get ready for an insightful experience! 

 

Our “Cybersecurity Around The World” event is just around the corner, taking place on November 11th and 12th, 2025. 

 

This is your opportunity to level up your understanding of cybersecurity and connect with leading experts.

 

Discover all the details and the full agenda on our dedicated Landingpage <https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/cyseca-bosch/events-5928572826.html> . 

 

How to join us?

On-site: join us in person in Bengaluru (Adugodi) for an immersive experience and direct networking opportunities at our villages.

 

Online: can`t make it to Bengaluru? No problem! We`re offering a free online livestream of three different stages, allowing you to participate from anywhere in the world.

Here are just a few highlights you won`t want to miss:  

*	Video Message | Tanja Rückert 
*	Fireside Chat: "Securing the Enterprise: A Leadership Conversation on Cybersecurity" | Dattatri S R, Christoph Peylo 
*	Panel Discussion: “Cybersecurity across domains: common goals but different challenges" | Padmaja A R, Vembar Priyamvadha, Guruprasad S, Nasam Srinivasulu S
*	Inside the Incident: A Deep Dive into Our Internal Cyber Battles | Ingo Hoofdman, ​Somen Mukherjee
*	Fireside Chat: “When AI takes action - Security in the Age of Agents” I Christoph Peylo, Nasam Srinivasulu S 
*	Data Privacy and its impact on India I Vinayak Godse (Data Security Counsil)
*	Crowdsourcing CyberPeace and Cybersecurity I Major Vineet Kumar (CyberPeace Foundation)

 

…and many more sessions from cybersecurity & AI enthusiasts covering critical topics across automotive, healthcare, privacy and regulatory areas. 

 

This is a unique opportunity to ask your questions directly to cybersecurity experts across a wide range of security domains. Don't miss the chance to enhance your knowledge and network with peers!

 

We eagerly look forward to seeing you at the Cybersecurity Around the World event – whether in person or online!

 

Secure yourself. Protect us.

 

Your Event Orga Team

C/CY

 

 

 

Best Regards,

BGSW Marketing and Communications

Subject: BUSINESS TRAVEL CRITICAL : Apply for Citibank Corporate Credit Card Immediately!
Body:
Dear Colleagues,

To ensure seamless business travels and to align with standards towards bTravel system roll-out in Q2 2026, it is mandatory to apply for the Citi Corporate Credit Card which will be the desired mode of payments for all domestic and international business travels.

All active On-Roll Associates are eligible to apply for the Citi Corporate Credit Card as deemed fit.
Whether you have travel plans or not, please apply as the travel advance issuance through the Forex cards will be stopped.

*	To access the Citi Credit Card Application Process Guide – Click Here <https://connect.bosch.com/files/app/s/0BlQX5rKGoINDmb3B82pIDm1ljve> 
*	To access the FAQ’s and Best Practices Guide – Click Here <https://connect.bosch.com/files/app/s/3Y3Q54EP99TYWk0ljPPOF5oz7dlW> 

*	For queries or clarifications, please email to BoschIN.CitiCreditcardSupport@in.bosch.com <mailto:BoschIN.CitiCreditcardSupport@in.bosch.com> 
*	If you have already applied or hold an active Citi credit card, then please do not re-apply.


	 	
 	


	

Best Regards,
Travel2Expense service (GS/HRS92-IN) – Credit Card Operations Team

Bosch & Indian Steel Supplier Collaboration: Experts Visit Indian Steel Plants to Explore Advancements and Future Rediness         

Indian Steel plants are investing for capacity enhancement from 205 million tonnage to 300 million tonnage by 2030 along with the adoption of advanced technologies to improve product quality, consistency, process efficiency & CO2 footprint. Bosch approved Alloy steel producers are already in process of investments include re-melting facilities such as ESR (Electro Slag Remelting), VIM (Vacuum Induction Melting), and VAR (Vacuum Arc Remelting), which help achieve cleaner steel with reduced inclusions to meet high pressure products(CP4,CP4iME,High pressure injectors pump,etc).

Material experts Dr.Moalla and Dr.Marcel visited our steel mills to witness the new state-of-the-art facilities such as re-heating furnaces, induction hardening and tempering units, and hot rolling mills. These upgrades collectively enhance process stability and yield consistency of quality requirements.

In Addition, they have also invested in R&D and quality analysis equipment's like ;ultrasonic immersion testing, scanning electron microscopes (SEM), and eddy current testers to enable precise defect detection, microstructural evaluation, and surface integrity assessment These technological advancements has a strong focus on competency development to effectively utilize these new technologies and sustain long-term quality excellence.

Panel Discussion: Open Innovation from Corporates

One of the highlight sessions was the panel on “Open Innovation in Action: Corporate Playbooks for Startup Success” in which Mohan Krishnaswamy (MS/EED-VM MS/KAM-PE-VM BGSW/PJ-NE-COB) shared his insights on how corporates can meaningfully engage with startups.  Some key takeaways / reflections from that discussion :-

*  Mindset matters: For corporates, viewing startups as collaborators.

*  Structures & governance help: Having internal frameworks lowers friction and accelerates engagement.

*  Transparency and trust: Clear communication on expectations, IP, roles, and metrics is critical.

*  Pilot-first approach: Experiments, proofs-of-concept, and minimal viable integrations often pave the way for deeper collaboration.

*  Ecosystem connectivity: Corporates benefit by plugging into startup ecosystems (incubators, accelerators, events) to stay ahead technologically and access new ideas

This helps signal to startups that corporates can be flexible, open, and co-creative, and gives corporates a chance to hear from the startup side about what they truly value (speed, clarity, communication, freedom to innovate).

Why This Matters (and What This Means Going Forward)

*  The Marketplace format accelerates discovery, conversation, and matchmaking. It turns passive interest into interactive engagement.

*  Innovation pitches allow startups to distill their ideas, get feedback, and capture attention.

*  Panel & thought leadership sessions help shift mindsets and set direction — by showing how open innovation can be operationalized, rather than just talked about.

*  For Bosch, being present in all these formats signals commitment — to listening, learning, partnering, and scaling with the broader ecosystem.

Platforms like TNGSS strengthen the bridge between industry and the startup ecosystem, accelerating the journey from ideas to impactful solutions.

We’re thrilled to invite you to the AI First Developer Day – powered by MongoDB and hosted in partnership with AWS <https://events.mongodb.com/developerdayboschindia> , on November 25, 2025, in Bangalore.

Subject: Key Amendments | Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) Policy
Body:
#ChampioningInclusion!

 

At BGSW, we are committed to building a workplace where every individual feels valued, respected and belonged. Our Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) Policy <https://kor2vm0022.apac.bosch.com/stages/#/workspace/702/_vv/process/guidance/_ZFJ-oL2bX2edQ4gg0PJQlg>  is at the core of this commitment, ensuring fairness and equity for all associates across every stage of employment.

 

In line with our DEI (Diversity, Equity & Inclusion) ethos and evolving workplace needs, we have introduced a few important amendments to the EEO Policy. These updates further strengthen our efforts to create a safe, inclusive and equitable work environment for all.

 

Key Amendments:

*	Transportation Support for PwD Associates: Revised clause includes provision for reasonable accommodation in shuttle routes and alternate solution due to non-availability of low-floor vehicles. It also includes transport assistance during dark hours for all associates.
*	Appointment and Role of Liaison Officer: The Liaison Officer’s updated responsibilities and contact details are now included in the policy.
*	Grievance Redressal & Non-Retaliation for PwD associates: A clearer grievance handling process with defined timelines and documentation, led by the Liaison Officer. The policy also includes a non-retaliation clause to encourage associates to confidently raise concerns.
*	Inclusion of EmpowerAbility ARG <https://teams.microsoft.com/l/channel/19%3A53wk7r0fvRZw6UAY_eNXx6V8UWgFHI3giKBSNBfcPmc1%40thread.tacv2/General?groupId=6285b9ff-9b6e-4957-8435-a9bebecdd3e9&tenantId=0ae51e19-07c8-4e4b-bb6d-648ee58410f4>  (Associate Resource Group): The EmpowerAbility ARG’s core team has been formally recognized as the disability inclusion working committee.

 

We encourage you to read the updated policy on Proview <https://kor2vm0022.apac.bosch.com/stages/#/workspace/702/_vv/process/guidance/_ZFJ-oL2bX2edQ4gg0PJQlg> .

 

Together, let’s continue to create an environment where equal opportunity is not just a policy, but a lived reality for everyone at BGSW.

 

	
 

 

If you have any questions or need further clarification, please reach out to @Sahu Seema (BGSW/HRL-DEI) <mailto:Seema.Sahu@in.bosch.com>  or @Rashmi C R (BGSW/HRL-CBP1) <mailto:Rashmi.CR@in.bosch.com> 

	




 

Mit freundlichen Grüßen / Best regards,

 

Unity Square – BGSW Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Team

24th October 2025

From Your Desk to Our Pages

Got a story that deserves the spotlight?

 

Here’s your chance to tell it and get featured in the next edition of BGSW Spectrum!

 

Pick a theme that fits your story:

*	The Power of Being in Progress - When “done” isn’t really the end.
*	The Hidden Experiments - Behind-the-scenes trials that shaped success.
*	Chaos as a Catalyst - Turning unexpected changes into creative solutions.

 

Deadline: October 24, 2025 | ✍️ Word Limit: 800–1000 | 🚫 No AI generated content

BGSW Cob Center Head Mr. Naved Narayan in 𝐏𝐚𝐧𝐞𝐥 𝐃𝐢𝐬𝐜𝐮𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐨𝐧 “𝐁𝐞𝐲𝐨𝐧𝐝 𝐌𝐞𝐭𝐫𝐨𝐬: 𝐓𝐚𝐤𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐀𝐈 𝐭𝐨 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐇𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐭 𝐨𝐟 𝐈𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐚” #FIT.KovAI 

At CII Southern Region Connect 2025 in Coimbatore, discussions around AI and emerging technologies underscored Tamil Nadu’s strong innovation momentum.

The Hon’ble Minister for IT & DS, Dr. P Thiaga Rajan announced the establishment of a 2 million sq.ft. Centre of Excellence for Artificial Intelligence at Coimbatore — aimed at skilling youth and fostering applied innovation.

He also highlighted the State’s leadership in AI adoption through initiatives like Tamil Nadu Technology Hub (iTNT) and India AI Mission partnerships.

Various Industry leaders discussed how AI can drive inclusive growth beyond metros, empowering India’s tier-II and tier-III cities to become engines of innovation and opportunity. The session highlighted Coimbatore’s emergence as a key hub for engineering excellence, GCC growth, and AI-driven development, underscoring the region’s growing contribution to India’s digital future.

“Tamil Nadu is emerging as a leader in GCCs, with 1 in every 5 in the country being set up here - and Coimbatore leading with exceptional talent,” said Mr Kewyn George (AI Futurist), Global IS Director & GCC Head, Expeditors International B.V.

“I’d put Coimbatore over any place in the world - the culture, stability, and team spirit here are unmatched,” remarked Dr Ankineedu Velaga, Managing Director, Yield Engineering Systems.

“To bridge the gap between today and tomorrow, we must focus on transferable skills like problem-solving and communication,” shared Ms Mahima ., Site Leader & Senior Director, Blue Yonder (Coimbatore Hub).

“AI enabled product engineering will be a true value add, and Coimbatore is setting the stage for world-class innovation in core engineering,” emphasized Mr Naved Narayan, Vice President, Mobility Solutions & Head – R&D Center, Bosch Global Software Technologies.  At Bosch Global Software Technologies, we remain committed to supporting such transformative initiatives that strengthen collaboration, accelerate innovation, and build a future-ready Tamil Nadu.


 


 








"Are technology, compliance, and innovation related? Is regulation a guardrail, or can it become a growth driver?..."  Questions reflected on at the CII Global Leaders Summit at Chennai says Mr. Naved Narayan, BGSW Cob Center Head         

As India moves forward with it's GCCs leading the way, the next frontier isn’t just technology or talent, it’s trust!

1. Compliance as a Design Principle:  Tech Leaders are embedding it into the design itself, asking, "Is this explainable? Is this consented?", creating simpler, resilient systems that scale globally across diverse regulatory regimes.

2. Innovation Through Constraint: Treating emerging data & AI laws as not barriers, but creative constraints pushing teams to design privacy-proof architectures, with low-data AI models, and transparent decision frameworks.

3. Trust as a Market Advantage, "Digital trust is the new currency.":  Done right, compliance becoming a growth accelerator, shaping stronger brands & loyal ecosystems.

At Bosch we see this exemplified by our initiatives such as, SmartFactories, IoT, and Automation initiatives, driving innovation safely and responsibly,  Programs securing AI/ML systems against adversarial risks, preparing for emerging standards like the EU AI Act & NIST frameworks, compliance is Becoming an Engineering Discipline

With the DPDP Act in India & the EU AI Act, we’re entering a world where:

- Legal and tech teams co-create compliance by design.

- Privacy & AI engineering practices such as differential privacy, federated learning, model interpretability becoming part of standard development pipelines

- Compliance automation tools continuously monitor data flows, consent, and model behavior

This is a new approach in how we build technology itself.   The Next Regulatory Turning Point will be the convergence of AI governance and data sovereignty.

GCCs that evolve to responsible innovation & growth centers embedding ethics, privacy, and accountability by design will define the next decade of global leadership.

Because the next wave of tech regulation won’t just constrain innovation it will differentiate those who can innovate responsibly.

"Global Capability Centers: Catalysts for 
Innovation in Manufacturing” Mr. Naved Narayan, BGSW Cob Center Head at the CII 15th Conclave on Manufacturing Innovation in New Delhi. 
#FIT.KovAI 

It was a privilege for Mr Naved Narayan, Vice President, Mobility Solutions & Head – R&D Center, Bosch Global Software Technologies to join technologists, innovators, and industry leaders at the CII 15th Conclave on Manufacturing Innovation in New Delhi.

The conversations on “Global Capability Centers (GCCs): Catalyst for Innovation in Manufacturing” reaffirmed one thing, India’s GCCs are already the innovation engines for the world.

At Bosch, this journey has deep roots.

For over 140 years globally, and 100+ years in India, we’ve built our foundation on product engineering and manufacturing excellence.

Our GCC, has played a pivotal role in building technology for India and bringing technology to India.

🔹 From pioneering technologies such as Common Rail Diesel systems in passenger cars to today’s ADAS and Software-defined Vehicle architectures, we’ve always looked at how technology can move industries forward.

🔹 The innovation journey doesn’t stop at proof-of-concepts or prototypes, it begins when we design for Robustness, Reliability, Manufacturability, and Scale. That’s where GCCs play a critical role bridging product innovation with real-world use.

🔹 As geopolitics, technology, and sustainability reshape global manufacturing, GCCs are bridging global innovation with local engineering strength

Looking ahead, Mr. Naved stated that he believes India’s GCC ecosystem will be instrumental in designing the next generation of products: made in India, engineered for the world.  Credit goes to Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) for bringing together such a powerful conversation on the future of tech & innovation-led next-gen manufacturing.


 


 






CXO Networking Breakfast @ BGSW #ManaHyderabad 

On 17th October, Bosch Global Software Technologies – Hyderabad proudly hosted the CXO Networking Breakfast, organized by HYSEA. The session was led by our Centre Head, Amjad Khan Patan, and brought together senior leaders from across the IT industry for an engaging discussion on collaboration, innovation, and growth.

The conversations focused on key topics such as member-engagement priorities, talent development, IT infrastructure, traffic management, and a joint CSR approach — all centered around the collective goal of strengthening Hyderabad’s growing IT ecosystem.

Leaders also exchanged ideas on accelerating the city’s IT growth and explored ways to collaborate with Government, Academia, and Industry to drive sustainable progress.

The event saw active participation from eminent industry leaders, including:
Prashanth Nandella (President – HYSEA), Phani Pattamatta (COO – HYSEA), Prashanti Bodugum (Evernorth Health Services – Head of Innovation Hub), Venugopal Kandimalla (ZELIS Healthcare India), Sriram Sundaram (People Prime Worldwide), Rama Bandlapally (Vialto), Visweswara Rao (Arcadis), Krishna Reddy (Amnet Digital), and Isaac Rajkumar (RealPage).

👏 A big thank you to HYSEA and all participants for fostering open dialogue and collaboration — reinforcing Hyderabad’s position as one of India’s fastest-growing innovation hubs.


 


 






#TribePune | Compassion, Creativity, and Wildlife Care: CSR Volunteers Make a Difference

As part of a CSR initiative focused on wildlife care and rehabilitation, volunteers visited RESQ, an animal rescue and rehabilitation center dedicated to supporting injured and displaced wildlife.

During the visit, volunteers interacted with the RESQ team to understand the organization’s operations, including treatment, recovery, and rehabilitation processes. They also toured various facilities, such as the insect breeding room, where insects are raised as feed for birds.

The group observed the care being provided to a parakeet, a python, and a rescued cheetah cub, gaining insight into the challenges and successes involved in wildlife rescue and rehabilitation.

In addition to learning activities, the volunteers contributed by creating enrichment tools for the animals. They built a wooden ladder for monkeys and designed a bird perch using PVC pipes and artificial grass-simple yet useful additions to the animals’ environment.

The initiative fostered awareness and understanding of wildlife conservation while strengthening teamwork and community engagement among volunteers. It concluded with participants expressing appreciation for the opportunity to contribute to a meaningful cause and support RESQ’s ongoing efforts in wildlife protection.

Subject: Our Gratuities Policy & Reporting Guidelines
Body:
Our Gratuities Policy and Reporting Guidelines

 

Dear Boschlers,

 

This email serves as an important reminder of our commitment to ethical conduct and compliance with our company's policies regarding gratuities, including the giving and receiving of gifts. Maintaining a high standard of integrity is fundamental to our values and critical for preventing conflicts of interest and ensuring fair business practices.

 



Understanding Gratuities

 

A gratuity, in the context of our policy, refers to:

 

“A tangible or intangible benefit to which the recipient has no legal entitlement. The ben-efit can be granted directly or indirectly (via a third party) to the recipient.”

 

Examples of direct benefit: gifts (including Bosch products), invitations to business lunches, professional events (trade fairs, seminars, lectures, etc.), entertainment events (cultural or sporting events, evening events, excursions, etc.), payment of travel and accommodation costs, use of a private holiday apartment, personal discounts.

 

Examples of an indirect benefit (so-called third-party benefit): Provision of an internship for a relative, donation to an institution or organization (e.g., association) close to the recipient.

 

Note: It is also a gratuity if a contract is concluded with the only purpose of formally legitimizing the benefit. For example, a staged contract for the free use of a business partner’s holiday home.

 



Why is this Important?

 

Even small gestures can create perceptions of undue influence or obligation. Our policy is designed to protect both the company and individual employees from potential ethical dilemmas, reputational damage, and legal repercussions.

 



Key Principles to Remember

 

•        Avoid Conflicts of Interest: Do not accept or offer gratuities that could improperly influence business decisions or create a perceived obligation.

 

•        Transparency is Key: When permissible gratuities are exchanged, ensure they are reported as per our guidelines.

 

•        Local Laws & Regulations: Always be mindful of and comply with applicable local laws and regulations concerning bribery and corruption, which may be stricter than internal policies.

 



Reporting Guidelines: Our Dedicated Tool

 

To ensure transparency and compliance, all reportable gratuities (both given and received) must be logged using our designated internal tool. This tool provides a secure and standardized method for documenting these interactions, allowing us to maintain accurate records and monitor compliance effectively.

 

You can access the Gratuities Reporting Tool here: WorkON <https://rb-wam.bosch.com/WorkOnDashBoard/search/search.seam?appKey=RBCM>  Dashboard | Gratuities <https://rb-wam.bosch.com/WorkOnDashBoard/search/search.seam?appKey=RBCM> 

 

Please remember that proper use of this tool is mandatory for all reportable instances. If you are unsure whether a gratuity needs to be reported, it is always best to exercise caution and report it or consult with the C/CMR-BGSW-IN.

 



Where to Find More Information?

 

We strongly encourage all employees to familiarize themselves with the full Gratuities Policy. This document provides comprehensive details on what is permissible, what is prohibited, reporting thresholds, and the approval process for exceptions.

You can review the complete Gratuities Central Directive and related compliance documents on our intranet:

*	C-Directive 06300 – Prevention of Corruption – Link <https://rb-wam.bosch.com/socos-rb/SOCOS/documents/ccm01/cd/10070/CD-06300-000_VAW_N_EN_2025-01-01.pdf> 
*	C-Directive 03200 – Attachment 1: Public Officials in India – Link <https://bgn.bosch.com/FIRSTspiritWeb/wcms/wcms_rgap/media/01_rgap/bosch_in_india/organization_84/rbin_1/organisation_1/corpfunctions/compliance_2/documents_219/CD-03002-001_ANH_N_EN_IN_2019-05-16.pdf> 
*	C-Directive 03200 – Attachment 2: Gratuities in Dealing with Third Parties – Link <https://bgn.bosch.com/FIRSTspiritWeb/wcms/wcms_rgap/media/01_rgap/bosch_in_india/organization_84/rbin_1/organisation_1/corpfunctions/compliance_2/documents_219/CD-03002-002_ANH_N_EN_IN_2019-05-16.pdf> 

 

Your adherence to this policy is vital in upholding BGSW's reputation and our ethical standards.

 

If you have any questions or require clarification on any aspect of this policy, please do not hesitate to contact C/CMR-BGSW-IN.

 

Thank you for your continued commitment to integrity and ethical conduct.

 

 

Sincerely,

C/CMR-BGSW-IN

Subject: Registration Open | Live online API Development Training on November 17-18
Body:
Dear colleagues,

 

Following the successful launch of our online API training courses in EMEA, 

We are now offering a brand-new hands-on API development online course in India from November 17 to 18, 2025.

 

Course Title:

[IT-API-Build-Experience-WN] Building and Experience APIs (Combined Program)

 

Course Overview:

This course is practice-driven and provides a systematic introduction to the full lifecycle of Bosch internal APIs. It focuses on key aspects such as:

*	API design, development, testing
*	API Security fundamentals
*	API Gateway configuration
*	API Marketplace management and publishing on Bosch-provided or certified platforms

*         

Participants will design and build an API from scratch, learning the complete process from writing API Specification documents to coding implementation and functionality testing.

The second part of the course will focus on API deployment and management, including how to configure Bosch internal API Gateway and API Marketplace. Through hands-on exercises, learners will configure Bosch’s internal API gateway to securely expose APIs to external networks and cloud platforms, while also gaining insights into Bosch’s API publishing, maintenance, and usage mechanisms.

By the end, participants will fully understand Bosch’s internal API design and delivery process from both a developer’s perspective and a consumer’s perspective, establishing a professional and systematic approach to APIs.

 

Training Objectives

After completing this training, you will be able to:

*	Design and write API Specification documents according to Bosch standards.
*	Implement and test API functionality with code.
*	Implement basic API security testing principles like OWASP Top Ten and so many others.
*	Deploy and publish APIs to the Bosch API Gateway and Bosch API Marketplace.
*	Maintain and monitor deployed APIs.

 

Training Format

*	Type: Live Online training
*	Dates: November 17–18, 2025 (2 days total)
*	Cost: 20900 INR per participant
*	Registration deadline: November 10, 2025
*	Location: MS Teams
*	Registration link: 499528 <https://performancemanagerrot.successfactors.eu/sf/learning?destUrl=https%3a%2f%2fbosch%2eplateau%2ecom%2flearning%2fuser%2fdeeplink%5fredirect%2ejsp%3flinkId%3dSCHEDULED%5fOFFERING%5fDETAILS%26scheduleID%3d499528%26fromSF%3dY&company=BOSCH> 

 

 

Target Audience

Bosch employees who are interested in API development and have basic IT skills.

 

If you would like to gain a deeper understanding of API development and strengthen your practical application skills in real projects, please register soon - spots are limited!

 

For registration or inquiries, please contact:

*	Sajib Chandra Ghosh (BD/DPA-GOI7)
*	SUN Jason (BD/DPA-GOI7)
*	Raymond Francis (BTC-IN)

 

We look forward to your participation!

 

Regards,

GS/HRS3-IN

Subject: ISP Awareness: Secure Conferencing tips -Recording and Transcription functions in MS Teams
Body:
Dear All,

 

In case we require to record or transcribe an MS Teams meeting, a best practice would be to notify all presenters and speakers in advance and obtain their consent. Detailed explanation is given below.

 



Recordings and transcriptions in MS Teams offer numerous advantages: they make content accessible even after the meeting, support precise documentation, facilitate the follow-up of complex topics, help absentees get comprehensive information, make trainings reusable, and much more. Overall, these functions significantly contribute to the quality and sustainability of collaboration. But they must be used compliantly and securely.



Using the ‘Recording’ function, the entire meeting can be recorded and saved with both image and sound (video). A transcript is also automatically created. The ‘Transcription’ function only converts the speech to text and does not generate a video. This function can be used independently of a recording function. Both recordings and transcripts could contain personal data and should hence be handled responsibly.

Important principles for organizers of a recording or transcription:

Create transparency: Inform all participants before you start a recording or transcription and obtain their consent – both are permitted only with prior consent (especially of presenters and speakers)! 

Act with purpose: "For security reasons" is not a valid reason! Record or create a transcript only if it is truly necessary.

Minimize data: Advise participants to turn off their camera and microphone if they do not wish to be recorded or have a transcript of their spoken words created. Also, make participants aware that they should refrain from sending messages in the chat.

Store securely: Recordings and transcripts belong exclusively in approved Bosch systems, not on your desktop or private clouds.

Delete in a timely manner: Recordings and transcripts are not archival documents. As soon as the purpose for which the recording or transcript was created has been fulfilled, delete them.

All the technical details about recording and transcription in MS Teams are available in BD-Docupedia <https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/spaces/NGW/pages/1268969056/Recording+Transcription> .

Tool preference:

Always use MS Teams recording option for recording and transcription. 3rd party tools are not recommended.

For info on requesting for the record permission role, refer Link <https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/spaces/CI4U/pages/1929708459/How+to+record+a+meeting+in+MS+Teams> .

Subject: The Weekly Wrap 31st October 2025
Body:
31st October 2025


 






SAP and Intel Japan Host Successful Smart Factory Tour at Bosch Bengaluru

On October 8, SAP and Intel Japan jointly organized a factory tour in Bengaluru, India, offering participants an inside look at Bosch’s state-of-the-art smart factory. The visit included an introduction to the Bosch Experience Center, live demonstrations of MES 4.0 and IIoT applications, and a Gemba walk through the Bidadi plant. Participants praised the event for providing practical, on-the-ground insights into digital manufacturing and for showcasing tangible progress in smart factory initiatives. The tour received highly positive feedback and marks a significant step forward in advancing SAP and Intel Japan’s smart factory strategy.


 


 





AI Kiosk @ BGSW MultiMarket: Embracing GitHub Copilot and making AI tool usage a culture         

The BGSW MultiMarket Unified Talent Family launched the AI Kiosk on October 28th, representing the AI-First strategy at MM. Designed to enhance productivity and efficiency, the event showcased how GitHub Copilot can be seamlessly integrated into associates’ daily workflows. Adopting a Gemba-style approach, the kiosk was activated at each floor across locations enabling hands-on interaction and engagement. Over 300 associates participated in the AI Kiosk across all locations. Associates facing challenges with Copilot integration, usage clarity or understanding its guardrails found immense value through live demos and project-specific discussions. The feedback was overwhelmingly positive, with participants recognizing Copilot as a powerful companion in their day-to-day delivery.


 


 






Strengthening Global Collaboration: Cybersecurity Process Assessment and Engagements between the Cybersecurity Office at BGSW and C/CYG GP (Governance for Products)

In a significant step toward deepening global collaboration, senior cybersecurity experts Dr. Lutz Bernd and Aktas Hakan from C/CYG GP visited India in October 2025 to engage with Anitha R Y & team from the Cybersecurity Office (CSO) for BGSW and RBIN. This initiative reflects the growing synergy between C/CYG GP and CSO to strengthen cybersecurity practices at One-BGSW and RBIN.

The first leg of the visit spanned with comprehensive cybersecurity assessments conducted on sample products of BGSW and RBIN. The outcome of the assessments was Zero Major non-conformities with few OFIs.  The Project Managers and Security Managers received additional information on the practices stated in CD 09000.

Knowledge-Sharing and Strategic Insights

Dr. Lutz Bernd led an impactful session covering:

*	The Cybersecurity Lifecycle (CD 09000 <https://rb-wam.bosch.com/socos-rb/SOCOS/documents/ccy01/cd/10050/CD-09000-000_VAW_N_EN_2025-01-01.pdf> )
*	The Cyber Resilience Act <https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/spaces/SG/pages/2431659859/EU+Cyber+Resilience+Act+CRA>  (CRA), 
*	The EU AI Act <https://eur-lex.europa.eu/resource.html?uri=cellar:e0649735-a372-11eb-9585-01aa75ed71a1.0001.02/DOC_1&format=PDF> 
*	Key takeaways from recent global assessments

This session drew participation from over 100 professionals across BGSW and RBIN, including Product Owners, Security Managers, Project Managers, and BDOs, underscoring the community’s strong commitment to continuous improvement. An exclusive interaction was held between the C/CYG team and the Mobility Software cybersecurity community (from PS, VM, and XC), offering a deep dive into the cybersecurity practices adopted in BBM projects.

The visit concluded at the EC 360 office, where focused discussions took place between the visitors and Rency Abraham (C/CYE MS/ECR) & team, particularly around endpoint protection and vulnerability tracking. The Security Operations Center (SOC) lab tour was organized for the visitors to gain first-hand insights into the operations supporting Bosch World.


 


 








BGSW #ManaHyderabad Strengthens Commitment to Inclusion through Assistive Tech Start-Up Screening        

On October 29, 2025, BGSW Hyderabad, in collaboration with T-Hub, hosted the Assistive Tech Start-Up Screening event — a significant milestone under our “Assistive Tech to the Last Mile” project. The initiative aims to promote technology-enabled inclusion for Persons with Disabilities (PwD) and advance our broader vision to influence inclusive policies in India, starting with Telangana.

The session was led under the guidance of Amjad Khan Patan, Shilpa, and Niraj, with active participation from Ravi Madan N, Praneeth Kumar Kotagiri, and Magapu Vamsi N V K, who served as part of the Bosch jury panel. Their thoughtful evaluations and deep technical insights helped identify scalable and impactful start-up solutions.

The jury also included representatives from the Government of Telangana — Smt. Shailaja, Director, Department for Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, Senior Citizens & Transgender Persons — alongside experts such as Ritesh Modi (AI/ML Specialist, Microsoft & T-Hub Mentor) and members from T-Works and the Telangana Government Innovation Cell (TGIC).

A total of nine start-up pitches were evaluated, out of which three to five will be selected to advance to the next phase. The final list will be announced at the Telangana Assistive Tech Summit on December 3, 2025, marking the International Day of Persons with Disabilities (IDPD).

This initiative reflects Bosch’s unwavering commitment to social impact, innovation, and inclusive technology, empowering communities through meaningful collaboration between industry, government, and start-ups.

Agile Dojo for Leaders & Practitioners @ BGSW #ManaHyderabad

This week’s Agile Dojo brought together both leaders and practitioners for a powerful learning experience focused on deepening agility through hands-on practice and reflection. Conducted on 27th & 28th October for practitioners and 29th October for leaders, the sessions created an inspiring space for collaboration, experimentation, and growth.

Session Highlights:

Agile Leadership in Practice: Leaders explored how to embody agile values, nurture psychological safety, and empower teams to take ownership.

Practitioner Engagement: Participants engaged in immersive simulations, applying agile principles to real-world challenges focused on iterative delivery and customer feedback.

Collaborative Synergy: Cross-role conversations helped bridge understanding and align common goals.

Mindset Evolution: Teams reflected on shifting from output-based to outcome-driven thinking, embracing experimentation and learning from setbacks.

Tools & Techniques: Hands-on sessions with Kanban boards, user story mapping, and value stream mapping helped visualize work and improve flow. The dojo reinforced that agility is not just a methodology — it’s a mindset and a culture. The energy, insights, and collaboration throughout the week have laid a strong foundation for the next phase — focusing on agile metrics and value-driven delivery.

A big thank you to all participants for making the Agile Dojo a space for learning, growth, and transformation! 


 


 








Visit by BD HR Leader Anne Kathrin Gebhardt @ BGSW Hyderabad

This week, we were delighted to host Anne Kathrin Gebhardt (BD/HR) from Germany at our BGSW Hyderabad Centre. Her visit provided a wonderful opportunity for learning, collaboration, and alignment across global teams.

During her visit, Anne engaged in a focused group discussion with the Hyderabad BD team members, gaining valuable insights into their experiences, challenges, and aspirations. She also met with BD Leadership at Hyderabad — Krishna Kishore Amara (BD/SPB-APB11), Nalla Sateesh (BD/EAC-IN), and Arun Kumar Palaniappan (BD/PJB-CEM) — along with location leaders Prakash Gadgi (BGSW/OFE-ECH-HYD) and Priya Menon (BGSW/HRL-BP-HYD).
These interactions helped her develop a deeper understanding of the Hyderabad ecosystem, the strengths and capabilities of the BD associates, and the significant role the BD team plays in driving success from this location.

A key highlight of Anne’s visit was her interactive session with the Women’s Community – She Rise, where she shared her personal leadership journey and insights on career growth, mentorship, and building support systems. Her reflections on diversity and empowerment left participants truly inspired and motivated.

The visit reinforced Bosch’s commitment to fostering collaboration, inclusion, and leadership excellence across borders.

#TribePune | Dive into the World of Service House India

A new episode of ADDA is here! Kuldeepak Chaudhari (MS/EAV1-PS) sits down with Santosh Battur (Service House Head & Section Head for ECS-PS) for an engaging conversation on high-performance culture, hybrid & EV markets, AI adoption, and growth opportunities. Plus, hear his personal story and enjoy some rapid-fire fun!

Sneak Peek:
