Body:
07th November 2025


 






Accelerating Secure ECU development with the CycurHSM Assistant by VM Vietnam 

Developed by BGSV-MS/ETA-SEC team and first piloted in 2024, the CycurHSM Assistant is an intelligent virtual expert designed to simplify and enhance embedded security solutions for automotive ECUs. Housed in Devmate, it supports the development and troubleshooting of complex cybersecurity software in Steering projects.  

The CycurHSM Assistant is hosted within Devmate, Bosch’s AI-powered workspace that streamlines workflows across domains. Whether you are a developer, project manager, or security engineer, Devmate offers a unified platform for accessing knowledge, automating tasks, and collaborating across teams. Devmate is built to reduce cognitive load, improve consistency, and accelerate development through intelligent automation.  

 <https://connect.bosch.com/blogs/978a83a6-7a0d-4e55-a0af-6bd1da6376a8/entry/Accelerating_Secure_ECU_Development_with_the_CycurHSM_Assistant?lang=en_us> Read more  >> 


 


 








Process Skill Hub: Learning together, growing together – an Initiative by MS/EPX-VM         

Process Skill Hub was launched by MS/EPX-VM to drive cross-functional learning, knowledge sharing, and collaborative problem-solving. Programs under this initiative cover key areas such as Agile and ASPICE coaching, Splunk and AssessPro training, and sessions on Q-Gates, 8D, and Value Stream Mapping. 

The team is planning to take this initiative forward to identify and address process pain points reported by Coaches and EQMs through process audits, Gemba walks, and analysis of missed KPIs from Splunk dashboards. Based on case studies, they share learnings and best practices to drive effective issue resolution. It also aims to ensure clear understanding of Implemented high-impact PCRs and PURE ideas, and effective knowledge sharing across teams. 

 <https://connect.bosch.com/blogs/978a83a6-7a0d-4e55-a0af-6bd1da6376a8/entry/Process_Skill_Hub_Learning_Together_Growing_Together?lang=en_us> Read more  >>

Agentic AI in Automotive: Six lessons from the industry by Shenoi Rajesh R (MS/EAX-VM, MS/EPX-VM) 

Agentic AI is transforming automotive software by enabling intelligent agents to streamline workflows, enhance safety, and boost efficiency. Shenoi Rajesh R (MS/EAX-VM, MS/EPX-VM) shares six key lessons shaping scalable human-agent ecosystems in safety-critical automotive systems. He also emphasis, in automotive AI, engineers won’t disappear—they’ll evolve into AI orchestrators. Calibration experts will supervise adaptive agents, system architects will set boundaries, and validation engineers will train agents to detect corner cases. User interfaces—visual dashboards, traceable decision trees, and simulation visualizers—will make this human-agent partnership seamless. 

Read more <https://connect.bosch.com/blogs/4d9b6eac-b365-4e10-8c59-9c061b4a8dea/entry/Agentic_AI_in_Automotive_Six_Lessons_from_the_Industry?lang=en_us>   >>


 


 






BGSW MultiMarket at AI Fusion Summit 2025 

Bhaskara Srihari V (SX/ETS-MM SX/PJ-GenAI-MM) and Verma Prakash (SX/EES-MM SX/EPS-MM SX/EPS1-MM) from BGSW MultiMarket represented Bosch at the AI Fusion Summit held in Kakinada. The event was organized by the Andhra Pradesh Digital Transformation Institute (APDTI) and the DeepTech Naipunya Foundation and is recognized as the official pre-summit event for the India-AI Impact Summit 2026, an international summit hosted by the Government of India.

Bhaskara Srihari delivered a keynote address on “Beyond Text: Multimodal GenAI for Vision, Speech, and Video”, highlighting the evolution of multimodal generative AI and its industrial use cases, followed by a fireside chat. 

Verma Prakash presented a keynote session on “The Robotic Senses Revolution: Vision, Touch, and Multimodal Perception”, highlighting how this multimodal fusion is transforming automation into intelligent collaboration for next generation robotics. 

The summit witnessed participation from over 1,000 attendees, including professionals from industry, academia, and students, fostering vibrant discussions on the future of artificial intelligence and its applications.


 


 





Bosch SDS Showcases Digital Solutions for a Sustainable Future at Convene4Climate

On 17th October, our Nordic Head of Software & Digital Solutions, Heidi Mills, took the stage at Convene4Climate in Rotterdam. The event brought together innovators, policymakers and business leaders who are driving action against climate change. In her session, Heidi shared how Bosch Software & Digital Solutions uses technology, AI and cross-industry collaboration to create measurable climate impact. She emphasized that true innovation happens when diverse perspectives come together and combine digital tools with human collaboration to scale sustainability solutions. The conference inspired valuable discussions on the role of partnerships and digital transformation in accelerating the green transition, and it was great to see Bosch SDS actively contributing to this important conversation.


 


 






IGNITE Community Celebrates Two Years of Creating Next-Gen Leaders

The IGNITE Community recently celebrated its second anniversary with an inspiring outing held last Sunday - marking two impactful years since its inception in September. What began as a platform to nurture innovation has now evolved into a movement to create next-generation leaders who drive change with purpose and collaboration.

The celebration was filled with team activities, reflections, and moments of gratitude, capturing the essence of what IGNITE stands for - learning, leading, and growing together.

Sharing his thoughts, Bellur Mohan Nanjundiah (BGSW/HRL-LCG BGSW/HRL-BP5 BGSW/HRL-FHE), said:

“We make a wonderful cohort, and I am convinced IGNITE is no longer just a cohort of people - but a tribe of leaders and change-makers who are definitely going to make the world a better place to be in.”

With strong participation from Coimbatore associates, IGNITE continues to grow as a vibrant community that connects minds, cultivates creativity, and celebrates collaboration.

As IGNITE steps into its next chapter, it continues to carry forward its mission - to inspire leadership, foster innovation, and ignite the spark within every individual.

IGNITE - Beyond Horizons. 🔥

✨ Want to be part of IGNITE?

Click here <https://connect.bosch.com/communities/service/html/communitystart?communityUuid=d04561c0-5bc2-4d05-9cf5-2a037e6fda94>  to join the community and start your journey of growth and leadership.


 


 






MS/ETO-SWC Leadership Connect Across Locations

Building Confidence Through Conversations

“Transformation is most powerful when it’s personal — when leaders and associates meet, listen, and inspire each other toward a shared vision.”

As part of fostering collaboration within the newly formed MS/ETO-SWC – Skill Hub for Engineering Tools, the leadership team visited Coimbatore, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and Pune to engage directly with associates.

Led by Biju T K, Cluster Director, along with Cluster Managers Anket Kumar, Mruthunjaya Reddy L, and Sudharshan Annamalai, the sessions reinforced SWC’s vision, addressed queries, and built confidence.

HR BPs Anand Anushka, Farheen Sultana Syeda, Chintamani Neha, and Dilip Verma joined to clarify people topics.

These connects strengthened trust, alignment, and belief in the SWC journey

Conversations that inspire confidence — MS/ETO-SWC leadership team meet associates across locations to listen, engage, and strengthen collaboration.


 


 





#TribePune | Gurukul - A Veerangana Initiative: Fostering Growth and Empowerment

This week marked the successful launch of Gurukul, a unique mentorship program powered by the women associates of #TribePune, stemming from the Veerangana initiative. Spearheaded by Deshmukh Geetanjali (SX/EVS3-MM M/BDX-GT2-O2C), Desai Madhuri Venkatarao (SO/OPM41-IN), Shekatkar Nupur P (GS/PUI2-AP2), Gurukul aims to nurture, connect, and empower the community through one-on-one mentor-mentee partnerships, inspired by ancient Gurukul traditions.

The program, with its motto "Grow Together. Lead Forever," focuses on guided learning, knowledge sharing, skill development, empowerment, and community building. It offers significant value: mentees gain clarity and career growth, mentors refine leadership skills, and the organization cultivates collaboration and continuous learning.

The launch event featured addresses from Aditya Adavi, Center Head BGSW Pune and VP APAC SDS, who encouraged participants to maximize the initiative. Mentors and mentees also shared their motivations, with Divya Ashish (BGSW/ECH-PUN BGSW/PJ-ETX-CoE-SY) highlighting her positive experience as a mentee at BGSW. This new initiative promises to be a vital platform for professional and personal development within #TribePune.


 


 








BGSW #ManaHyderabad at PMI Pearl City Chapter – Sharing Insights on Human-Centered Leadership         

This week, Vamsi Magapu (BGSW/ETM3-HYD) from BGSW #ManaHyderabad delivered an insightful session at the PMI Pearl City, Hyderabad Chapter on “Human-Centered Leadership for Project Excellence.”

Drawing from his Vietnam Success Story, Vamsi shared how challenges around trust, communication, and cross-cultural collaboration transformed into a powerful journey of empowerment, ownership, and team alignment. He highlighted how structured leadership methods not only enabled change and transformation but also shaped his personal growth — a journey that earned him the Bosch Certified Product Engineering Leader (LFG) recognition in July 2025.

The session deeply resonated with attendees, who shared how the lessons and approaches discussed could be applied within their own teams. Vamsi emphasized that trust builds connection, clarity drives alignment, and adaptability sustains growth — timeless principles drawn from real-world leadership experiences.

👏 Congratulations to Vamsi for representing Bosch at PMI and inspiring leaders across the community to lead with empathy, clarity, and purpose.

🚀 "Know Your Products" Series: VM Steering Portfolio Deep Dive 

We are pleased to announce the continued success of the "Know Your Products" training initiative! Launched on April 29th as a cross-section collaboration between the MS/EBP-VM and MS/EBC-VM section heads, this program is designed to enhance cross-product expertise across our VM teams in Hyderabad, primarily targeting VM associates to strengthen their technical and product knowledge. This week marked the successful completion of the second session, which offered a comprehensive look into the VM Steering domain product portfolios, providing a structured learning experience where participants dove deep into the products' Working Principles, traced their Product Evolution from early forms to modern technologies, and highlighted the key Engineering Challenges that have been successfully addressed across successive product generations. We thank everyone who participated in this vital effort and encourage all associates to look out for details on the next session as we continue to explore the diverse and evolving landscape of VM products!


 


 






BGSW #ManaHyderabad Represents Bosch at GIRT Hyderabad

On 3rd November 2025, Bosch Global Software Technologies – Hyderabad proudly participated in the German Indian Round Table (GIRT) event hosted at ZF Tech Center India.
Our Centre Head, Amjad Khan Patan (BGSW/ECH-HYD), and Talent Lead, Vamsi Magapu (BGSW/ETM3-HYD) represented Bosch in this insightful forum that brought together industry leaders, academia, and government representatives to discuss India–Germany collaboration on talent mobility, skilling, and global opportunities.

The session started with valuable insights shared by H.E. Mr. Michael Hasper (Consul General of Germany, Chennai) on the evolving employment landscape in Germany and the role of Indian talent in strengthening the German economy

The event then continued with distinguished speakers mentioned below who shared perspectives on strengthening Indo-German partnerships through education, cultural exchange, and workforce development

Dr. Anjali Pande, Assistant Professor, EFLU Hyderabad for introducing the German language programs at EFLU and encouraging collaboration with Germanic Studies students.

Ms. Shaikh Shabna, Manager TOMCOM, from the Ministry of Labour and Employment for outlining government initiatives that support workforce transition from Telangana to Germany, including essential training programs with motto “Global Skills for Global Opportunities”

Ms. Amita Desai, Founder Director of Goethe-Zentrum Hyderabad, for emphasizing the importance of cultural and professional exchange.

👏 The event reinforced Bosch’s commitment to global collaboration, skill development, and nurturing future-ready talent


 


 





BGSW at ISIE – Indian Karting Race & Formula Imperial

BGSW sponsored the ISIE – Indian Karting Race (IKR) and Formula Imperial (FI) held at CoASTT High Performance Centre, Coimbatore in collaboration with BGSW/HRL-FHE.

The event brought together young engineering talent from across the country, showcasing innovation and passion for mobility. Our experts also contributed as technical inspectors and jury members, supporting the next generation of automotive engineers. It was an exciting collaboration that celebrated technology, teamwork, and the spirit of engineering excellence.

Among the 4 days event, the final day witnessed the Endurance test of the vehicles followed by the Awards ceremony, which was joined by Nanda Kumar C S (BGSW/ETX) & Bellur Mohan Nanjundiah (BGSW/HRL-LCG BGSW/HRL-BP5 BGSW/HRL-FHE).


 


 






Bosch India Plastics Techday 2025: Shaping Mobility & Beyond. Smart Materials & Manufacturing for sustainable Tomorrow.

The 9th Edition of Plastics Techday, held on 30th October at Bosch Adugodi campus was jointly organized by RB-CoC Platsics, 
IN | MS/NE-PG | MS/ENH-PLA & GS/MAC-AP2. The event paved the way for deeper collaboration between Plastic Experts, Engineering and manufacturing groups from various Bus, as well as Bosch partner organizations BASF & Autotech Sirmax.

This event marked a significant milestone, providing Bosch associates with an opportunity to exchange knowledge with experts from partner organizations through Marketplace & Deep Tech sessions. Session commenced with an inspiring and energizing talk from Mr. Shrikrishna, Technical Director (MS/ENH), how “ Collaboration, Innovation & Science come together- to shape the modern world. He emphasized the Key role of Plastics in driving efficiency & sustainability.  

The welcome address was delivered by Mr. Shrikanth P Hegde, Vice President - Product Engineering (MS/NE-PG MS/KAM-ME) who highlighted how plastics bring convenience and value to Industry and end users. 

The event was inaugurated by Mr. Guru Mallikarjuna, Senior Vice President - Mobility Solutions (MS/BE3 MS/NE-PS PS-SC/CE-AP) who lit the ceremonial lamp in accordance with Indian tradition, joined by other dignitaries on the dais. During his inaugural speech, Mr. Mallikarjuna emphasized the significant role of Plastics in achieving Carbon neutrality. He also highlighted how Techday fosters synergy & knowledge exchange across the ecosystem to collaboratively address challenges faced by the 
end user.

Keynote address by Mr. Nagendra H G, Regional Business Unit Head (PS-CC/RBU-IN) highlighted India’s leadership in delivering plastic products & solutions for Global markets. He also highlighted the importance of designing for sustainability and underscored collaboration as the way forward for well-engineered products. In his keynote address, Dr Kugele Daniel from Bosch Corporate Research Germany (CR/AMP2) shared insights on sustainable plastics and discussed the opportunities in
End-of-Life Vehicle Recycling, offering valuable perspective to Bosch associates.

A panel discussion on “Plastics as a Growth Driver” was moderated by Mr. Senthilmurugan B (MS/ENH-PLA), featuring panelists Mr. Pramod R (M/MBR-IN) from Bosch, Mr. David Vorgerd from BASF and Mr. R K Arora from SIRMAX.

120+ Bosch associates from BBM & MM BU’s and RO-IN plants like NhP1, ChkP, GanP participated in-person and 300+ associates joined the Bosch Tube live streaming across the globe. At Bosch, Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) are integral to our values, with Gender Diversity being one of our key focus areas. This program, conducted in collaboration with BTC-IN and Interweave Consulting, is tailored for women professionals with 1–6 years of total work experience. It empowers participants to tackle workplace challenges with greater confidence and capability through:

 

*	A one-day workshop
*	Post-workshop assignments
*	A 60-minute group nudge session to reinforce learning and application

 

As part of the learning journey, participants will also craft a personalized career action plan to drive both professional and personal growth.

*	Speaking Up with Confidence

Subject: What's Next for Cybersercurity Around the World #India2025 - See You Tomorrow!
Body:
Dear colleagues,

 

We hope you had a fantastic first day at the Cybersecurity Around the World #India 2025 event!

 

It was truly inspiring to see so many engaged and enthusiastic participants, and the energy at Adogudi and in our live stream was incredible. 

 





Your participation made it even more valuable!

 

But the excitement doesn't stop there! Day 2 is packed with even more opportunities for learning, networking, 

and growth.

 

We've got a fantastic line-up planned for tomorrow that you won't want to miss. Additional to the main stage you will find two further stages: Stage 2 “Cybersecurity and Mobility” and Stage 3 “Regulations & Data Privacy”: 

*	Streaming link Main stage Day 2  <https://bosch.mediaspace.de.kaltura.com/media/CyberSecurity+Awareness+Week/0_75pszjvy> >>> 
*	Teams link Stage 2 “Cybersecurity & Mobility”  <https://teams.microsoft.com/l/meetup-join/19%3ameeting_MGNmOTJkZGMtNDczOS00ZmVjLWJmZmYtNjIyN2RiMDVjNGY5%40thread.v2/0?context=%7b%22Tid%22%3a%220ae51e19-07c8-4e4b-bb6d-648ee58410f4%22%2c%22Oid%22%3a%223202b761-0924-451d-a9ce-e67b2d2cc53e%22%7d> >>>
*	Teams link Stage 3 “Regulations & Data Privacy”  <https://teams.microsoft.com/l/meetup-join/19%3ameeting_NTA3YjM1ODYtZjhmNS00MzgyLTk1NWUtZWIxOWI4YTAyN2Nh%40thread.v2/0?context=%7b%22Tid%22%3a%220ae51e19-07c8-4e4b-bb6d-648ee58410f4%22%2c%22Oid%22%3a%223202b761-0924-451d-a9ce-e67b2d2cc53e%22%7d> >>>

 

Need a refresher on tomorrow's schedule?

You can access the full Day 2 agenda  <https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/cyseca-bosch/agenda-6146901750.html#Agenda-Day2> >>here 

 

We truly value your presence and input. Your questions, insights, and engagement are what make the Cybersecurity Around The World #India 2025 a truly impactful experience. 

 

So, get ready for another day of inspiration and collaboration! We're looking forward to seeing you tomorrow, November 12th, 2025, starting at 10:30 am.

 

Best regards,

The C/CY Event Team 🦁

 

✅ To be even better in the future please share your opinion with us and fill out our short survey <https://boschci.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6Wr6isxoYBuL7j8> .

Subject: IMPORTANT: Policy updates effective Nov'25 - Leave & Effort Regularization
Body:
Dear Colleague,

 

We hope this message finds you well! We want to take a moment to remind you about our Bosch effort-based attendance system (BEST) guideline and Leave policy which ensures smooth operations and accurate payroll processing.

 

Key highlights of Leave policy revision effective Nov’25 is as follows:

 

1.	Unused General Leaves cannot be carried forward to the following calendar year. There will be no exception to carry forward all lapsable leaves to the following calendar year (including new joiners of 2025).
2.	Accumulated Earned Leaves in excess of 60 days will be automatically encashed by Jan’26 payroll instead of Mar’26.

Key highlights of BEST policy revision effective Nov’25 is as follows:

 

It is essential to book your efforts daily and submit weekly for approval in the Digital PPM solution - Planisware <https://rb-wam-ap.bosch.com/rbei-plw-prod/plw/collaboration/Time%20cards/TimeCard%20Input>  Additionally, you are required to plan your leave in advance and apply them pro-actively through Employee Self-Services (ESS). Failure to do so, could result in significant compliance and statutory impacts on retiral contributions, which we aim to avoid. In case you have missed the opportunity to update your efforts, the ESS tool must be used to book effort.

 

1.	No more waiting period (1 week) between closure of Timecard window <https://rb-wam-ap.bosch.com/rbei-plw-prod/plw/collaboration/TimeCard%20Due%20Date%20Details>  in the BGSW effort booking tool and enablement of Effort Not Booked (ENB) window in Employee Self-Services (ESS). Eg: For CW46 (09.11.2025 to 15.11.2025), the timecard window closes on 24.11.2025 and the ENB window will be enabled on the following day, that is, by 25.11.2025
2.	All pending leave requests (except ENB, Deputation, Business reason, Forgot ID) in the manager queue pertaining to previous month corrections will be auto-approved on the early hours of 24th calendar day of the month. ONLY ENB, Deputation, Business Reason, Forgot ID should be manually approved by the manager and within the monthly cut off date (23rd) to avoid payroll and / or Hybrid office presence impact to the associate.
3.	Failure to comply will result in missed days being recorded as 'blank' days (NRF) leading to payroll processing them as Leave Without Pay (LWP) and irreversible payroll deductions for the associate.

 

Managers/Timecard controllers – Please encourage your teams to book their effort on time. In the circumstances where associates have not booked effort, please ensure that the ENB is raised well in time for you to approve by the 18th of the month. Sufficient reminders between 18th to 23rd are being sent. Failure to approve leave or ENB requests by 23rd would result in disciplinary action.

 

For more information, please refer to BEST <https://kor2vm0022.apac.bosch.com/stages/#/workspace/705/_vv/process/guidance/_uhM00DGElBCG4_Vdp-zl2A>  and Leave <https://kor2vm0022.apac.bosch.com/stages/#/workspace/705/_vv/process/guidance/_MLUlAMzscWSqMYStzJkZsA>  policies. Further clarification (if any), please reach out to your respective HR-Business Partners.

 

Your cooperation is greatly appreciated.

 

Thank you for your attention to these updates.



 

Best Regards,

BGSW/HRL-CBP

Subject: Concern Regarding Delays in work Due to Team Member's Performance
Body:
Dear Sandhya,

 

I hope you're doing well.

 

I wanted to bring to your attention an ongoing concern regarding one of the team members Yudhajit whose recent performance has been affecting the progress of our current sprint. Unfortunately, he has been consistently delayed in completing assigned tasks, which in turn is impacting the ability of other team members to move forward with their work. As you know, many of our deliverables are interdependent, and these delays are creating a bottleneck, which is impacting the overall efficiency of the team.

 

I have had a couple of discussions with Yudhajit to offer support and understand any challenges he might be facing, but it seems the situation has not improved significantly. While I am committed to helping Yudhajit get back on track, I wanted to escalate this matter for your awareness and to discuss potential next steps in addressing this issue.

 

It would be helpful to have your input on how you'd like to proceed. Perhaps we could consider additional support or reassignment of tasks to ensure the team's momentum is maintained.

 

Please let me know if you'd like to discuss this further or if there's anything specific you'd like me to do in the meantime.

 

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

 

Best regards,

Rohith Kumar

Scrum Master, Capstone Project Squad-1

BGSW MultiMarket showcases the power of convergent innovation at Bengaluru Tech Summit 2025        

At the Bengaluru Tech Summit 2025, Guruprasad S (Vice President & Global Director, BGSW Multimarket) delivered a compelling keynote highlighting that the most impactful innovations arise from the convergence of technology, purpose, and creativity. He underscored how ambitious ideas often fall short when even one of these elements is missing, referencing examples like the Metaverse and Hyperloop, while showcasing UPI as a standout model where all three aligned to transform India’s digital economy. He also showcased Bosch’s Vivaray as a standout example of Indian innovation built for global impact, offering early anemia detection through painless, non-invasive screening, improving patient trust, and driving equitable access to diagnostics for rural communities. Addressing an audience of innovators and industry leaders, he emphasized that “Infinite Horizons” is more than a theme. It reflects a belief that the future belongs to innovations that are purposeful, imaginative, and truly transformative.

XC Tech Day 2025

The first-ever XC Tech Day 2025, held simultaneously across all locations(BAN- ADU, BAN ECU, COB, HYD and Pune) on November 12th and 13th, marked a significant milestone for One XC. With the theme “Transforming the Way We Do Engineering,” the event showcased our capabilities across SDM, SDI, AI-driven engineering, ADAS, compute platforms, and holistic AI frameworks for future vehicle systems. It reinforced how global efficiency combined with strong regional customization drives our vision of becoming the most preferred ADAS and Compute partner for OEMs in India. The day featured expert Tech Talks, panel discussions on Virtualisation, India Market Trends, and GenAI, along with a dynamic marketplace of demos and innovation pitches. Additionally, all pre-events culminated in a special award ceremony recognizing outstanding contributions. A heartfelt thank you to everyone for the exceptional coordination, teamwork, and enthusiasm that made this event a true success.


 


 








BGSW Multimarket at the CII Global MSME Business Summit 2025

At the CII Global MSME Business Summit 2025 organized by Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) in close collaboration with World Economic Forum (WEF), Mr. Guruprasad S (Vice President & Global Director, BGSW Multimarket) delivered sharply focused insights on how MSMEs can evolve from local competitiveness to global relevance through technology-led transformation. Speaking on the panel “Digitization, Automation & AI,” moderated by Archana Bhatnagar (MD, Haylide), featuring Mr. Koustabh Kulkarni (Siemens Digital Industry Software), and Mr. Dattatraya Navalgundkar (MD, C4i4 Lab) along with Mr. Guruprasad S. He outlined a pragmatic three-step adoption pathway of Digitize, Automate, Apply Machine Intelligence, positioning it as a scalable blueprint for MSMEs. He also highlighted Bosch’s dedicated MSME solutions such as DeviceBridge, Indus, ctrlX, Deepsights, and AI offerings, emphasizing their role in accelerating operational maturity. A compelling case study on using Agentic AI to predict fashion trends and optimize textile capacity planning showcased the tangible impact of AI-driven decision-making. He also stressed the importance of the “AI Playbook for MSMEs” as a practical, ready-to-adopt guide, reinforcing that purposeful and structured technology adoption will be key to unlocking the next wave of MSME growth.

BGSW MultiMarket Industrial4.0 team (SX/EBI-MM) charts the future-proof strategy  

A pivotal workshop bringing together BGSW MultiMarket's Industrial4.0 team along with a strong consortium of horizontal practices: Product Engineering (SX/ENA-MM), Data and AI (SX/EDS-MM), Application Engineering (SX/EAE-MM) and Cybersecurity (SX/ECY-MM) led by Tripathy Deba Prasad (SX/EBI-MM). The session focused on reflecting on 2025 and strategically increasing BGSW's presence within BBI GBs and regional functions, identifying areas for greater responsibility.

A central theme woven throughout the deep discussions was the transformative power of AI to leverage and generate unparalleled value for Bosch BBI Business Units. This collaborative spirit led to the development of a robust three-year strategy, meticulously aligned with Bosch BBI's core focus areas. The strategy embraced a "Save for Growth" philosophy, powered by diversified levers along with aggressive expansion in key regional growth markets like India, North America, and Japan, in close partnership with GBs. Asset-led growth emerged as another critical focus, ensuring direct value generation at the GB product level. Beyond internal growth, the workshop underscored the importance of BGSW influencing the wider industry through thought leadership in the industrial sector, supported by a strong communication strategy for both internal and external engagement.


 


 






PRODEYSSEY 2025

Dear Team,

Prodeyssey 2025 has been an incredible journey across Bangalore, Coimbatore, and Pune—far beyond an event, it became a celebration of our shared vision for the future of product engineering in both mobility and non-mobility sectors. This year’s edition came alive through engaging sessions, technology showcases, and thought-provoking discussions.

*	Shrikanth P Hegde (Vice President of NE-PG)

Celebrating the Spirit of Giving: Daan Utsav 2025 at Bosch        

This year’s Daan Utsav at Bosch was a true testament to the power of collective goodwill. Across four locations—Bangalore, Coimbatore, Hyderabad, and Pune associates came together to make a meaningful difference through two impactful initiatives.

The Blood Donation Drive saw an overwhelming response, with 281 associates donating blood: Bangalore (113), Coimbatore (114), Hyderabad (15), and Pune (39). Each unit donated is a testament of compassion representing a life potentially saved .

Equally inspiring was the Virtual Volunteering effort, where 24 associates collaborated to create question-answer banks for students with visual impairments. By reviewing and translating 24 chapters into regional languages, they enabled accessible learning through assistive technology.

Daan Utsav 2025 was more than a campaign; it was a celebration of empathy, inclusion, and the Bosch spirit of giving back. Together, we proved that small acts can create lasting impact !

GS India Town Hall 2025 – WINGS of Progress

With the year drawing to a close, GS India recently hosted its biggest event of the year, the GS India Town Hall 2025. Centered around the theme of digitalization and AI, the event celebrated India’s growing influence as a global digital reformer. As the very pillars driving global transformation mirror GS India’s own evolution from process enablers to strategic partners: the internal strategy, WINGS for Bosch 2030, was also introduced and spotlighted. Reflecting the alignment of external inspiration with internal ambition, the Town Hall theme, “WINGS of Progress: Powered by People and Driven by Digital,” perfectly captured the spirit of the day. The event witnessed the enthusiastic participation of over 1,000 GS India associates, coming together to connect, collaborate, and celebrate. The day was filled with networking, key business updates, captivating cultural performances by colleagues, and the much-awaited Rewards & Recognition ceremony, honoring outstanding contributions in 2025. Adding to the excitement, Joerg Mimmel (GS/EP), Executive Vice President, Global Business Services, joined the celebrations and even took the “hot seat” to answer some thought-provoking questions from associates. Overall, the event was a true reflection of India’s collaborative spirit, innovative mindset, and the shared drive to succeed as one GS India team.


 


 








BGSW-CII-IWN Will Writing Session

BGSW, in collaboration with CII-IWN, recently organized a virtual session on “Effective Will Writing “that witnessed participation from over 330+ associates. 

The session was conducted by Ms. Anjali Prabhakaran, who provided comprehensive insights into estate planning.

Key Topics Covered

The session addressed six essential aspects of Will writing. Participants learned what constitutes a Will—a legal declaration for distributing assets after one's demise—and understood important legal terms like testator, beneficiary, executor, and witness.

Ms. Anjali explained the requirements for a valid Will, including sound mental state, voluntary execution, clear identification of beneficiaries and assets, executor appointment, and proper witnessing. Associates discovered that any person of sound mind above 18 years can create a Will, regardless of marital status.

The session also covered the flexibility to revoke or modify Wills through new documents, codicils, or destruction of the original. Practical guidance on storage options—with family, executors, banks, lawyers, or through registration—concluded the informative session.

This initiative reflects our commitment to holistic employee welfare, addressing crucial personal financial planning needs beyond workplace benefits.

100 Days of SWC Success: A Hyderabad Townhall Recap!

ENG-SWC recently celebrated a remarkable 100-day milestone with a series of events culminating in a high-energy townhall in Hyderabad. This pivotal gathering united all ENG-SWC Directors, including Julius Panakkal, to chart the organization’s future.

The townhall served as a strategic blueprint, with leaders outlining clear directions across key pillars: boosting Efficiency, deepening Associate Engagement, and strengthening Competency Building. Achievements from the past 100 days were showcased, highlighting collective success.

Further enriching the session, Site HRBPs Priya Menon and Farheen Sultana provided essential HR updates, while Amjad Khan Patan, Site Head of BGSW HYD, delivered an inspiring address that resonated with all present.

The presence of the entire SWC HYD organization, alongside Hyderabad Cluster Managers, created an atmosphere of vibrant enthusiasm and camaraderie. Leaders eagerly engaged with SWC associates, addressing their questions and fostering a collaborative spirit. This open dialogue further solidified the sense of unity and shared purpose within the Hyderabad SWC family. This event truly encapsulated the spirit and ambition driving ENG-SWC forward.

Here's to many more milestones and continued success! .


 


 








BGSW #ManaHyderabad at T-Health Café, CIE – IIIT Hyderabad Campus | Advancing Innovation in MedTech and Diagnostics

Amjad Khan Patan, Centre Head – BGSW Hyderabad, represented Bosch at the T-Health Café hosted at the CIE, IIIT Hyderabad campus. The event brought together thought leaders, innovators, and healthcare entrepreneurs to discuss the future of MedTech innovation and diagnostics in India.

In his address, Amjad highlighted how Bosch Global Software Technologies continues to bridge engineering excellence with healthcare innovation. He spoke about emerging trends shaping India’s diagnostics sector, including precision medicine, digital diagnostics, and point-of-care technologies that are redefining patient outcomes. He also emphasized how Bosch fosters startup engagement through accelerators, hackathons, and technology scouting initiatives, nurturing early-stage innovation and collaboration within the healthcare ecosystem.

Amjad further underlined the importance of demonstrating clinical validation, scalability, and integration readiness, which are critical for any healthcare innovation to achieve real-world impact. He shared Bosch’s journey in healthcare technology — from building robust engineering capabilities to creating meaningful solutions in diagnostics, connected devices, and digital health platforms.

Concluding his talk, Amjad shared his vision for India as a hub for affordable, scalable, and globally competitive diagnostic innovation, reinforcing Bosch’s commitment to advancing healthcare access and empowering MedTech startups to shape the future of diagnostics and patient care.

Building Agile Leaders @ #ManaHyderabad – ALDP Convocation

On 13th November 2025, BGSW Hyderabad celebrated the successful culmination of the Agile Leader Development Program (ALDP) — a unique initiative by ATO, organized in collaboration with T-Hub. Launched in April, the program ran through six sessions from May to August, bringing together 18 participants from diverse roles and functions. ALDP went beyond traditional agile training — focusing on “Being Agile” rather than just “Doing Agile.” Participants developed agile leadership competencies through hands-on learning, covering topics such as flow-based systems, problem-solving, design thinking, creative thinking, and value stream mapping.

The convocation, hosted at BGSW Hyderabad, featured an inspiring external talk by Mr. Rajashekhar (Quality Director, Amgen), who shared his real-world experience in applying problem-solving to develop sustainable agricultural solutions. A key highlight during the program was a guest session by Mr. Ankireddy Praveen, who shared practical insights into agile thinking and leadership from his professional journey.

A heartfelt thanks to Amjad Khan Patan, Centre Head – BGSW Hyderabad, for his continued vision and support in fostering leadership development and agile culture at #ManaHyderabad. Special appreciation to Pitchala Shashikala (BGSW/PJ-ETA-H BGSW/PJ-ETA-ITD) and the Talent Management Team – Hyderabad (Sujana Sree Majji) for their efforts in enabling ATO to host this program successfully. Kudos to all our certified Agile Leaders for their enthusiasm, commitment, and innovative problem-solving! And a big thank you to Dinesh Roy L (BGSW/ETT BGSW/PJ-ETT-ETB), Sreeja Bhargavan (BGSW/ETA), Dolly Christina (BGSW/PJ-ETA-PTQ), Udupa Parameshwara E G (BGSW/QMM-PM), and Subbaramu G (BGSW/QMM-PM, MS/QMM) for championing and driving the agile movement across our ecosystem. The success of ALDP once again reinforces that agility is more than a method — it’s a mindset to create lasting business impact.


 


 








#TribePune | EVC-CV | Advancing Functional Safety Through Expert Training

The EVC-CV Pune team successfully hosted a high-impact functional safety training led by Florian Moldenhauer, Functional Safety Manager (XC-CE/ESC). This program empowered our EVC-CV and NE2-XC Pune associates with advanced safety expertise, further strengthening our product development, risk management, and compliance capabilities.

Florian’s ability to simplify complex safety principles and connect them to daily engineering practices provided associates with actionable insights into risk identification, assessment, and mitigation. This helps us to consistently meet the highest global safety standards.

In discussions with Pune Business SPOC Ramesh Palaniappan (BGSW/PJ-ESO1-PUN) and Sahu Nishant (MS/EVC-CV1-XC), Florian recognized the team’s expertise and engagement at Pune, which adds value for our strong positioning for future market readiness in the IOEM ecosystem, which the EVC-CV team continues to strengthen.

XCite Tech Day at Pune

XCite Tech Days was an exciting and engaging event that brought together multiple business units at the stalls. 

XC-Pune was proud to showcase XC products and portfolio to business heads and associates across different BUs. Stalls on GenAI, ADAS for India, Project Excellence, Common Framework, XC Efficiency, and other initiatives reflected the XC theme and product flow. 

The day featured interactive discussions on use case clarity, product technical content, and valuable exchanges of project experiences and collaboration models. From the inaugural session to the Stall Winner announcement, the energy remained high, with Tech Connect via Bosch Tube adding further insights through innovation highlights and panel discussions.

Overall, it was a day of bold interactions, boundless pride, and collaborative spirit that energized the entire XCite Tech Day.


 


 






Building Agile Leaders @ HYD

ATO along with T-Hub organized the Agile Leader Development Program (ALDP) at BGSW Hyderabad. Pitchala Shashikala, who as the T-Hub lead @ HYD was instrumental in having this program. Mahadev and Ravindra from ATO started this program in April and had six sessions from May – Aug where over eighteen participants from distinct roles and functions from Hyderabad center participated. ALDP is more than just a training, it is a coaching intervention which focuses on Agile Leader competencies. The program focused beyond the general agile training, going from doing Agile to Being Agile where the intention was to develop an Agile Mindset focusing both on Agile and Behavioral topics. The topics included the development of a flow-based system, Flow Accelerators, Problem Solving, Design thinking to arrive at ideas using How Might We technique, Value Stream Mapping, Creative Thinking. One of the key highlights of learning was a guest talk from Mr. Ankireddy Praveen who gave us key insights of Agile thinking from his professional journey. The participants had to work on a problem statement from their projects and the results were presented to their managers which was well appreciated. 

The certification ceremony was conducted on Nov 13, which was a culmination of the efforts from all the participants. The event started with an invocation from Reshmasree Lankalapalli and was well conducted by Preeti Donepudi. Mahadev gave an overview of the ATO and ALDP journey @ HYD. The highlight of the program was an external talk from Mr. Rajashekhar Totad who is the Quality Director at Amgen. He took us on his problem-solving journey where he was responsible of developing a product for increasing the yield of crops with limited water resources. The talk was very insightful and gave us a good example of applying how problem solving was applied in farming domain. Patan Amjad Khan as center head of HYD was incredibly supportive of this program, his inspiring words is motivating for us to start the next competency development programs. The happy faces of the participants along with a momentum was satisfying to see the successful culmination of the fifth edition of ALDP.

A Huge Thanks to all our Agile Leaders who participated, presented their solutions, and held their certificate with pride and made the whole program successful!

A special thanks to those who actively contributed to the success of these programs and continue to drive the Agile movement forward; Dinesh Roy L (BGSW/ETT BGSW/PJ-ETT-ETB), Mrs. Sreeja Bhargavan (BGSW/ETA),  Dolly Christina (BGSW/PJ-ETA-PTQ), Pitchala Shashikala (BGSW/PJ-ETA-H BGSW/PJ-ETA-ITD) for supporting all Agile initiatives at T-Hub.

Udupa Parameshwara E G BGSW/QMM-PM BGSW/QMM-PM-MAT) and Subbaramu G (BGSW/QMM-PM, MS/QMM) for championing Agile culture with a focus on business outcomes.

Agility is more than Process, Methods, and Tools, it is a mindset to create business outcomes. With programs like ALDP, AMDP, PODP, Growth Mindset Bosch is ensuring that leaders of today are ready for the challenges of tomorrow.

Subject: IMPORTANT: Policy updates effective Nov'25 - Leave & Effort Regularization
Body:
Dear Colleague,

 

We hope this message finds you well! We want to take a moment to remind you about our Bosch effort-based attendance system (BEST) guideline and Leave policy which ensures smooth operations and accurate payroll processing.

 

Key highlights of Leave policy revision effective Nov’25 is as follows:

 

1.	Unused General Leaves cannot be carried forward to the following calendar year. There will be no exception to carry forward all lapsable leaves to the following calendar year (including new joiners of 2025).
2.	Accumulated Earned Leaves in excess of 60 days will be automatically encashed by Jan’26 payroll instead of Mar’26.

Key highlights of BEST policy revision effective Nov’25 is as follows:

 

It is essential to book your efforts daily and submit weekly for approval in the Digital PPM solution - Planisware <https://rb-wam-ap.bosch.com/rbei-plw-prod/plw/collaboration/Time%20cards/TimeCard%20Input>  Additionally, you are required to plan your leave in advance and apply them pro-actively through Employee Self-Services (ESS). Failure to do so, could result in significant compliance and statutory impacts on retiral contributions, which we aim to avoid. In case you have missed the opportunity to update your efforts, the ESS tool must be used to book effort.

 

1.	No more waiting period (1 week) between closure of Timecard window <https://rb-wam-ap.bosch.com/rbei-plw-prod/plw/collaboration/TimeCard%20Due%20Date%20Details>  in the BGSW effort booking tool and enablement of Effort Not Booked (ENB) window in Employee Self-Services (ESS). Eg: For CW46 (09.11.2025 to 15.11.2025), the timecard window closes on 24.11.2025 and the ENB window will be enabled on the following day, that is, by 25.11.2025
2.	All pending leave requests (except ENB, Deputation, Business reason, Forgot ID) in the manager queue pertaining to previous month corrections will be auto-approved on the early hours of 24th calendar day of the month. ONLY ENB, Deputation, Business Reason, Forgot ID should be manually approved by the manager and within the monthly cut off date (23rd) to avoid payroll and / or Hybrid office presence impact to the associate.
3.	Failure to comply will result in missed days being recorded as 'blank' days (NRF) leading to payroll processing them as Leave Without Pay (LWP) and irreversible payroll deductions for the associate.

 

Managers/Timecard controllers – Please encourage your teams to book their effort on time. In the circumstances where associates have not booked effort, please ensure that the ENB is raised well in time for you to approve by the 18th of the month. Sufficient reminders between 18th to 23rd are being sent. Failure to approve leave or ENB requests by 23rd would result in disciplinary action.

 

For more information, please refer to BEST <https://kor2vm0022.apac.bosch.com/stages/#/workspace/705/_vv/process/guidance/_uhM00DGElBCG4_Vdp-zl2A>  and Leave <https://kor2vm0022.apac.bosch.com/stages/#/workspace/705/_vv/process/guidance/_MLUlAMzscWSqMYStzJkZsA>  policies. Further clarification (if any), please reach out to your respective HR-Business Partners.

 

Your cooperation is greatly appreciated.

 

Thank you for your attention to these updates.



 

Best Regards,

BGSW/HRL-CBP

Subject: The Weekly Wrap 14th November 2025
Body:
14th November 2025


 






#TribePune | CSR Spotlight | Building Community Through Creative Expression 

Our volunteers recently teamed up with our CSR partner, Leadership for Equity (LFE), for a wonderfully uplifting day at Kharalwadi Primary School.

They helped students from Grades 5 to 7 create greeting cards to thank someone special in their lives. The classrooms buzzed with excitement as kids poured their emotions into colorful cards for parents, teachers, and friends. 

In the end, over 80 vibrant cards were made, each a powerful expression of thankfulness. It was a beautiful blend of fun and learning. The activity was a step toward nurturing empathy, fostering emotional wellbeing, and gratitude. 

This truly showed the impact when organizations like LFE and BGSW come together – we're not just building things, we're nurturing empathy and igniting creativity in these bright young minds. 


 


 





Active Campus | Digital Art

As part of the Active Campus initiative on 13th Nov, Boschlers at the Adugodi campus had the opportunity to immerse themselves in the fascinating world of Digital Art through an engaging and insightful session conducted by Janjo Jose Kollannoor (BD/TOA-PLM3) — an exceptionally talented artist known for his creative flair and expertise in digital illustration.

During the session, Janjo introduced associates to the endless possibilities that arise when art and technology come together. He demonstrated techniques to merge traditional artistic expression with digital tools, guiding Boschlers on how to create visually stunning pieces using modern platforms and software.

The session offered a fresh perspective on how digital art can be both expressive and accessible, encouraging associates to experiment with new creative methods and explore their artistic potential beyond conventional mediums.

It was truly inspiring to see Boschlers blend imagination with innovation — embodying the spirit of Active Campus, where learning, creativity, and community come together in harmony.

Up Next:

The creative journey continues with our next session — “Post and Paint” — scheduled for 27th November at Adugodi Campus. Get ready for another colorful and inspiring experience where art takes center stage!


 


 






XCite: Celebrating Innovation and Collaboration at BGSW- Hyderabad 

On 12th November 2025, Bosch’s Hyderabad campus came alive with XCite – the XC-Tech Day, a vibrant showcase of innovation, collaboration, and cutting-edge technology.

The event featured eight marketplace stalls, each highlighting innovative solutions and technologies developed by Bosch associates. The marketplace served as a platform to demonstrate solutions, exchange ideas, and inspire cross-domain collaboration, reflecting Bosch’s strong culture of innovation.

XCite embodied the spirit of “Invented for life,” encouraging associates to explore, engage, and be inspired by their peers’ creativity while reinforcing Bosch’s commitment to a future-ready innovation ecosystem.

Key Highlights

•      Mobility Cockpit Innovations: Showcasing IVI, ADAS, and Gateway technologies.

•      Strategic Focus: Addressing key technology challenges with actionable solutions.

•      Industry Insights: Leveraging Generative AI to meet evolving market needs.

XCite is more than an event — it’s a strategic platform that drives collaboration, accelerates innovation, and positions Bosch at the forefront of technological transformation in mobility and beyond.


 


 





Empowering Women Entrepreneurs – MoU with We Hub, A Govt of Telangana Initiative

On Monday, November 10, we took an exciting step forward in our commitment to fostering women’s entrepreneurship by signing a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with
We Hub. Through this collaboration, we aim to support the growth of women entrepreneurs by building and participating in programs that offer mentorship, technical guidance, access to resources, and opportunities for showcasing their work.

This partnership will also open doors for our associates to engage as mentors, nurture an entrepreneurial mindset, and co-create innovative solutions in the field of technology.

The initiative has been led by the She Rise community in Hyderabad, marking another milestone in our journey toward empowering women and driving inclusive growth.

In a world that shifts faster than ever, resilience isn’t optional anymore—it’s essential. This program invites participants to step out of the comfort zone, understand the human side of change, and build skills that support personal and interpersonal resilience.

 

If you’re ready to grow—or know someone who is—this is your opportunity.

Because resilience isn’t just a skill—it’s a superpower.

*	Handle stress and uncertainty more effectively
*	Acknowledge individual differences in change journeys
*	Develop a growth-oriented mindset
*	Strengthen personal resilience
*	Improve interaction and communication during change

Subject: Importance of Business Partner Compliance
Body:
Upholding Integrity in Our Business Relation with Intermediaries

 

Dear Boschlers,

 

At BGSW, conducting business with the highest standards of ethics and integrity is paramount and fundamental to our success and reputation. A key part of this commitment involves how we select, engage, and manage our business relationships with Intermediaries.

This communication serves as an important reminder of our shared responsibility to ensure these relationships are transparent, properly documented, and compliant with all applicable laws, including anti-bribery and anti-corruption regulations and Bosch Group Directives.

 

Why is this so important?

Intermediaries, while often essential to our business operations, can also pose significant legal and reputational risks and may expose BGSW and our employees to severe penalties, including large fines and even criminal liability. A robust due diligence and risk management process is our first line of defence.

 

Your Role and Responsibilities

Every OE involved in engaging or managing Intermediaries must adhere to our company's established procedures. Key responsibilities include:

1.	Conduct Due Diligence: Before engaging an Intermediary, conduct an Integrity Check using the “Business Partner Due Diligence” (BPDD) tool and Risk Assessment to determine corruption risk and the appropriate level of due diligence. The diligence level aligns with the engagement's risk (low, medium, or high).
2.	Compliance Screening and Risk Mitigation: The Requestor must verify 'Alerts' against intermediary data from onboarding and evaluate risks ('Red Flags') identified during Risk Assessment, Due Diligence or Compliance Screening. They are then required to define, implement, and document appropriate mitigation measures for these identified risks.
3.	Approval: The Requestor may not obtain approval until all the process steps have been fully processed and completed. The responsible manager based on intermediary’s pre-determined corruption risk may approve or reject the business relationship with the Intermediary:

Risk level

Approvals required

Low

Responsible Manager

Medium

Responsible Manager + Subsequent recommendations and notes as needed by CPO

High

Superior Manager (Senior Management) + Subsequent recommendations and notes as needed by CPO

4.	Requirements for Drafting Intermediary Agreements: All Intermediary agreements must in writing and include:

	*	Detailed description of the services provided by the Intermediary
	*	Amount/ Calculation basis of the agreed remuneration
	*	Details on payment methods

Note: The payment of the remuneration in cash is inadmissible

	*	Invoicing, invoice verification and payment terms
	*	Compliance clauses
	*	Obligation to comply with the Code of Conduct for business partners
	*	Obligation to notify changes on the part of the Intermediary

5.	Speak Up: If you encounter any red flags or have concerns about a potential or existing relationship with an Intermediary, you have a duty to report it immediately to your manager, the Legal Department, or the Compliance Department. You can also use our confidential reporting platform – “Speak Up”. 

 

Key Definitions and Policies

For clarity, please refer to the following definitions and policies that govern our approach to working with Intermediaries. 

Definition of an Intermediary: Any person (natural person) or any company (legal person) commissioned to act on behalf of Bosch or to represent Bosch´s interests (e.g., consulting and support services in the initiation, negotiation and/or conclusion of contracts/orders or the application for licenses or permits).

*	Intermediaries in this sense are in particular (not exhaustively): sales intermediaries, commercial agents (in the sense of a sales assistant of Bosch), agents, brokers, representatives, freight forwarders (including border traffic and customs clearance), lobbyists, and other interest representatives.
*	No intermediaries within the meaning of this C-Directive are, in particular: customers (including resellers on their account), end customers, and suppliers. Furthermore, lawyers, tax consultants, and auditors are also not intermediaries (in this case, the respective existing Bosch order processes are to be applied). Legal entities of the Bosch Group and their associates are generally not intermediaries. Associates can be intermediaries if they act as such outside their employment contract with Bosch.

Applicable Policies and Procedures:

*	C-Directive 03010 "Business relations with Intermediaries of Bosch" – Link <https://rb-wam.bosch.com/socos-rb/SOCOS/documents/ccm01/cd/10070/CD-03010-000_VAW_N_EN_2022-08-01.pdf> 
*	Attachment 1 "Compliance Clauses" to C-Directive 03010 – Link <https://rb-wam.bosch.com/socos-rb/SOCOS/finder.cgi?CD-03010-001_ANH_N_XX> 
*	Attachment 2 "Detective Controls (DC)/Monitoring Procedures (MP)" to C-Directive 03010 – Link <https://rb-wam.bosch.com/socos-rb/SOCOS/finder.cgi?CD-03010-002_ANH_N_XX> 

 

Our Commitment

Compliance is a collective responsibility. By diligently following our procedures for engaging Intermediaries, you are not just protecting the company-you are protecting yourself and upholding the integrity that defines us.

 

Thank you for your continued dedication to doing business the right way.

 

If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to reach out to C/CMR-BGSW-IN.

 

Sincerely,

C/CMR-BGSW-IN



 

 

Best Regards,

BGSW Marketing and Communications

Subject: IMPORTANT: Policy updates effective Nov'25 - Leave & Effort Regularization
Body:
Dear Colleague,

 

We hope this message finds you well! We want to take a moment to remind you about our Bosch effort-based attendance system (BEST) guideline and Leave policy which ensures smooth operations and accurate payroll processing.

 

Key highlights of Leave policy revision effective Nov’25 is as follows:

 

1.	Unused General Leaves cannot be carried forward to the following calendar year. There will be no exception to carry forward all lapsable leaves to the following calendar year (including new joiners of 2025).
2.	Accumulated Earned Leaves in excess of 60 days will be automatically encashed by Jan’26 payroll instead of Mar’26.

Key highlights of BEST policy revision effective Nov’25 is as follows:

 

It is essential to book your efforts daily and submit weekly for approval in the Digital PPM solution - Planisware <https://rb-wam-ap.bosch.com/rbei-plw-prod/plw/collaboration/Time%20cards/TimeCard%20Input>  Additionally, you are required to plan your leave in advance and apply them pro-actively through Employee Self-Services (ESS). Failure to do so, could result in significant compliance and statutory impacts on retiral contributions, which we aim to avoid. In case you have missed the opportunity to update your efforts, the ESS tool must be used to book effort.

 

1.	No more waiting period (1 week) between closure of Timecard window <https://rb-wam-ap.bosch.com/rbei-plw-prod/plw/collaboration/TimeCard%20Due%20Date%20Details>  in the BGSW effort booking tool and enablement of Effort Not Booked (ENB) window in Employee Self-Services (ESS). Eg: For CW46 (09.11.2025 to 15.11.2025), the timecard window closes on 24.11.2025 and the ENB window will be enabled on the following day, that is, by 25.11.2025
2.	All pending leave requests (except ENB, Deputation, Business reason, Forgot ID) in the manager queue pertaining to previous month corrections will be auto-approved on the early hours of 24th calendar day of the month. ONLY ENB, Deputation, Business Reason, Forgot ID should be manually approved by the manager and within the monthly cut off date (23rd) to avoid payroll and / or Hybrid office presence impact to the associate.
3.	Failure to comply will result in missed days being recorded as 'blank' days (NRF) leading to payroll processing them as Leave Without Pay (LWP) and irreversible payroll deductions for the associate.

 

Managers/Timecard controllers – Please encourage your teams to book their effort on time. In the circumstances where associates have not booked effort, please ensure that the ENB is raised well in time for you to approve by the 18th of the month. Sufficient reminders between 18th to 23rd are being sent. Failure to approve leave or ENB requests by 23rd would result in disciplinary action.

 

For more information, please refer to BEST <https://kor2vm0022.apac.bosch.com/stages/#/workspace/705/_vv/process/guidance/_uhM00DGElBCG4_Vdp-zl2A>  and Leave <https://kor2vm0022.apac.bosch.com/stages/#/workspace/705/_vv/process/guidance/_MLUlAMzscWSqMYStzJkZsA>  policies. Further clarification (if any), please reach out to your respective HR-Business Partners.

 

Your cooperation is greatly appreciated.

 

Thank you for your attention to these updates.



 

Best Regards,

BGSW/HRL-CBP

Subject: The Weekly Wrap 28th November 2025
Body:
28th November 2025


 






Celebrating Men Who Make Work ‘Work’… @ BD/ERA-AMS-ASL Team

The year-end Team Connect began with a refreshing theme: Our Men, Our Strength, celebrating International Men’s Day by recognizing the often-unsung heroes who bring logic, humor, and steady support to our workplace. To honor them, the team organized a series of fun and engaging activities. The evening kicked off with a lively team-building game, “Helping Old McDonald Find His Animals,” followed by a creative challenge where the men crafted hearts from paper—an unexpectedly delightful showcase of their artistic side.

The most entertaining segment was the Cold Seat Round, where leaders answered humorous and surprising questions, revealing their playful personalities. The Emoji Reaction Challenge brought even more laughter as participants acted out joyful emojis.

The celebration ended with cake cutting and high tea, appreciating the contributions of the wonderful men across the organization. Impressively, the entire event was planned and executed by the women—a true Women4Men tribute.


 


 








BGSW MultiMarket Showcases Manufacturing 
Co-Intelligence at Bosch AI Day 2025        

At the Bosch AI Day held at the Bosch Centre for Artificial Intelligence (BCAI) in Renningen, the theme “Turning AI Technology into Life” set the stage for showcasing transformative innovations across the organization. BGSW Multimarket team made a strong presence with contributions from Palaniappan Balachandar (SX/ECI1-MM), Ayvarnam Nagarajan (SX/EFF1-MM), Gollapudi Krishna Chaitanya (SX/EDI2-MM), Vijay Manukonda (SX/EDI1-MM), Sharon A Neha (SX/EAL2-MM), Rajasekhar Reddy Kadasani (SX/EAL1-MM), Vandana R D (SX/EDI3-MM) for the HIT-007 project. Presented as Manufacturing Co-Intelligence, HIT-007 introduces a framework for Agentic AI in manufacturing aimed at democratizing AI adoption by offering ready-to-use AI agents and enabling rapid development of scalable, custom solutions rooted in Bosch’s deep manufacturing expertise.

BGSW MultiMarket leadership converges for a future forward blueprint

BGSW MultiMarket’s leadership came together today for a powerful convergence of ideas, alignment, and future thinking. Unified Talent Family Open House at BGSW Multimarket 

The Unified Talent Family recently hosted engaging Open House sessions in Bangalore and Hyderabad, creating a vibrant platform for dialogue, clarity, and collaboration. Led by our Talent Head, Mr. Ulindala Bala Suresh Reddy (SX/ETF-MM SDS/BSV SX/ETE-MM), the event brought associates together for meaningful conversations on vision, structure, and the evolving role of talent in shaping organizational excellence. The NASSCOM Technology Confluence (NTC) 2025

Coimbatore Edition brought the industry together under the theme “The Era of Intelligent Progress,” with Coimbatore, one of the 10 host cities, demonstrating how emerging tech hubs are reshaping the future of engineering and software innovation. Naved Narayan, Coimbatore Center Head joined a thought-provoking panel that explored the city’s expanding role in India’s technology landscape, the industry’s shift from AI experiments to impactful AI-driven experiences, and the growing potential of intelligent systems in domains such as autonomous marine navigation. Co-creation stood out as a defining theme, emphasizing the power of long-term collaboration between teams, partners, and GCCs, where shared expertise and joint problem-solving enable faster innovation and more meaningful outcomes.  At BGSW, we remain committed to this collaborative, engineering-led mindset as a catalyst for India’s next wave of digital transformation.

#TribePune | Shining a Light on Children's Futures: Volunteers Craft Solar Lamps 

This Children’s Day, our volunteers embraced a truly meaningful cause: assembling solar lamps for children in rural communities. Over the course of two impactful days, 110 dedicated volunteers came together to craft a remarkable 245 solar lamps, directly supporting rural children's education by providing much-needed sustainable lighting. 

The impactful initiative highlights our unwavering resolve to make a tangible difference in communities lacking reliable electricity, collectively brightening educational opportunities for children and helping pave the way for a better, more sustainable future.


 


 








#TribePune | BGSW and ARAI Collab for ADAS Data Collection        

BGSW Pune and MS/EPI-OE-XC teams, in collaboration with The Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI), have initiated ADAS India data collection this month onwards to capture diverse Indian driving scenarios and enhance our ADAS solutions for the local environment. This partnership leverages ARAI’s prior experience of 56,000 km of Indian road data capturing, including their expertise in navigating inter-state processes. With requirements primarily driven by BGSW, the path assignments, journey execution, and packaging of data back to Bengaluru are well aligned, and the activity is progressing smoothly. As the data collection nears completion, we expect to further strengthen and fine-tune our ADAS functions for Indian road conditions with valuable insights from this initiative.

The external keynote by Mr. Jay Dholakia, founder - skill verge, highlighted how a mindset shift among project managers is essential to thrive in this evolving landscape. The event featured insightful external speakers and a dynamic panel discussion with industry experts, including Renu Rajesh -President PMI Chapter, Pune and Vivek Sonar, Head IMCR Mahindra. Conversations centered on emerging challenges, the changing business environment, and the increasing role of AI tools. This productive exchange has successfully laid the groundwork for future collaboration, marking an impactful start to building strong SWC & BGSW-Pune alignment.

#TribePune | Highlights from the SAE Commercial Vehicle Electrification Conference

Dattatraya Ramchandra Kurade (BGSW/PJ-ESM-PUN) represented Bosch at the recent SAE Commercial Vehicle Electrification Conference in Pune. He was joined by Electrification PRM and System Engineers. Our presentation highlighted Bosch's comprehensive electrification product portfolio for the commercial vehicle segment, emphasizing the capabilities of our Indian organization in both engineering and production.

The conference served as a valuable forum for understanding perspectives from other Tier-1, Tier-2 suppliers, and Indian OEMs. Discussions included new battery technologies, advancements in motor and power electronics, and the status of localization efforts across the industry.

Additionally, our partners from ARAI presented insights into the legislative framework and available validation infrastructure within India.

Our involvement at the conference underscored our commitment to the advancement of sustainable mobility solutions for commercial vehicles, leveraging our expertise and local resources.


 


 








Nurturing Next-Gen Talent: Celebrating Interns & Apprentices Achievements

On 26th November, MiDAS organized a celebration event to recognize the outstanding contributions and achievements of our interns and apprentices.  MiDAS is actively engaging interns and apprentices as an integral part of the program, and their contributions have become strategic to driving innovation and accelerating delivery across the portfolio. The event brought together HRL, ETT, MiDAS leadership and mentors to witness presentations by each participant, showcasing their technical work, demos, learnings, and reflections.

MiDAS adopted an innovative model where interns and apprentices are distributed across sub-teams with shared responsibility balancing learning, research, and execution topics, each paired with dedicated mentors. This approach ensured they gained exposure to real-world challenges—from technical documentation and benchmarking to bug fixes and feature enhancements—while contributing meaningfully to live projects. Beyond daily tasks, they actively participated in MiDAS Round Table presentations and demos to GB leads, and featured their work in MiDAS Touch newsletters. They were also included in preparations for key conferences like BBM TechCon and ASPIRE AI, demonstrating how their work directly impacts the broader ecosystem. 

Participants expressed gratitude for being treated as regular team members and trusted with meaningful responsibilities. One apprentice shared, "MiDAS is like an extended family, and everyone patiently supported our learning journey amidst high project pressure." Mentors highlighted the energy and speed that the early talent brought into MiDAS, noting how often they could be seen exchanging learnings, passionately discussing tasks, and collaborating to solve problems. Mohan Bellur from HRL praised the initiative as a case study in how internships can be deeply integrated into live projects to enhance value. The MiDAS leadership team continues to champion this model as a scalable approach for nurturing future-ready skills while co-creating impactful solutions. MiDAS remains committed to being a launchpad where young talent and experienced teams shape the future together.

Manohar Yerraguntla, President, PMI Pearl City Chapter, delivered a compelling keynote that highlighted the shift from operational execution to strategic innovation. Vinay Babu Tarala, General Secretary, PMI Hyderabad Chapter, shared powerful insights on navigating today’s BANI world (Brittle, Anxious, Non-linear, Incomprehensible). He showcased practical ways PMs can leverage AI to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows, and elevate project delivery.

Panel Discussion: “Evolving PM Mindset for Business Impact”
A dynamic panel featuring Divya K, Nikhil Gupta Daram, and Praneeth Kotagiri, moderated by Vamsi Magapu, explored real-world experiences and strategies that help PMs create tangible business value and evolve as strategic contributors.

Guru Charan G., Susheel Kumar Gosangari, Monika, and Sai Kumar P. Satya.

and to our amazing volunteers — Chiranjeevi Maddi, Ravi Pandey, and Kalyan Nookala for capturing and supporting every moment of PM Week 2025.

A heartfelt thank you to all speakers, participants, and organizers who made this year’s PM Week a tremendous success.


 


 








Affordable Intelligence on Wheels” – India’s SDV Vision

This week, Bosch Global Software Technologies made a strong mark at the Auto EV Tech Vision Summit 2025 in Bengaluru, where our Center Head, Mr. Naved Narayan, joined an industry panel discussing the rapid transformation toward Software-Defined Vehicles (SDVs) in India.

Key takeaways from the session:

*  India is progressing rapidly toward connected, OTA-upgradable vehicles with Level 2+ ADAS becoming mainstream.

*  Two-wheeler ADAS and OTA capabilities are already proving market readiness.

*  AI-native zonal controllers optimized for Indian driving conditions are the next major milestone.

*  Connectivity and compute advancements (5G/6G, zonal & central architectures) will accelerate the journey to Level 3/4 autonomy.

*  AI-driven perception models, digital twins, and DevSecOps will define the future of vehicle intelligence.

A big thanks to the organizers and industry peers for the insightful exchange. The momentum behind India’s SDV evolution continues to grow, and we are excited to be part of shaping what’s ahead.

A Day of Creativity and Calm: Artistry Avenue at Cubbon Park

The Artistry Avenue community came together for a refreshing and inspiring art session at Cubbon Park, where Boschlers spent a beautiful day reconnecting with creativity, nature, and themselves. Surrounded by the park’s lush greenery and calming ambience, associates enjoyed a much-needed outdoor break from routine, allowing art to become their pathway to relaxation and mindfulness.

The session offered an open, welcoming space where everyone—beginners and experienced artists alike—could explore their creativity without pressure. With the rustling of trees, gentle sunlight, and the soothing energy of the surroundings, Boschlers immersed themselves in sketching, painting, and freehand expression. Many described the experience as grounding, therapeutic, and energizing.

Outdoor activities like this do more than spark creativity—they build community, reduce stress, and enhance overall well-being. Art in nature helps individuals slow down, breathe deeply, and reconnect with their inner calm, all while bonding with fellow associates in a meaningful way.

By the end of the day, smiles, colours, and stories filled the space. The Artistry Avenue event at Cubbon Park was not just an art session—it was a reminder of the joy that comes from pausing, expressing, and simply being present.

During his visit to BGSW #ManaHyderabad, our President, MD & CEO Datta Salagame joined the SHeRise women’s community for an engaging and inspiring lunch interaction.

A big thank you to Datta and all the women associates who participated and made this interaction impactful and energizing!

Bringing Back the Joy of Handwritten Love: Paint & Post at Active Campus

As part of the Active Campus initiative, a heartwarming Paint & Post session was conducted under the creative guidance of Apoorva Somshekhar Wadde. The event brought together 70+ Boschlers, each eager to pause, create, and reconnect with a timeless form of expression handwritten postcards. In an age dominated by screens and instant messages, the simple charm of writing a heartfelt note is often forgotten. Paint & Post beautifully revived this essence. Associates spent the session painting their own postcards - each one unique, colourful, and deeply personal. They poured their emotions onto paper through art, adding thoughtful messages meant for loved ones, friends, mentors, and even for themselves.

The energy in the room was vibrant yet calming. Boschlers explored colours, patterns, and stories, transforming blank cards into meaningful keepsakes. What began as an art activity soon turned into a nostalgic journey- one that reminded everyone of the joy of slowing down, creating something by hand, and expressing gratitude or affection in a way that feels truly personal.

Subject: IMPORTANT: Policy updates effective Nov'25 - Leave & Effort Regularization
Body:
Dear Colleague,

 

We hope this message finds you well! We want to take a moment to remind you about our Bosch effort-based attendance system (BEST) guideline and Leave policy which ensures smooth operations and accurate payroll processing.

 

Key highlights of Leave policy revision effective Nov’25 is as follows:

 

1.	Unused General Leaves cannot be carried forward to the following calendar year. There will be no exception to carry forward all lapsable leaves to the following calendar year (including new joiners of 2025).
2.	Accumulated Earned Leaves in excess of 60 days will be automatically encashed by Jan’26 payroll instead of Mar’26.

Key highlights of BEST policy revision effective Nov’25 is as follows:

 

It is essential to book your efforts daily and submit weekly for approval in the Digital PPM solution - Planisware <https://rb-wam-ap.bosch.com/rbei-plw-prod/plw/collaboration/Time%20cards/TimeCard%20Input>  Additionally, you are required to plan your leave in advance and apply them pro-actively through Employee Self-Services (ESS). Failure to do so, could result in significant compliance and statutory impacts on retiral contributions, which we aim to avoid. In case you have missed the opportunity to update your efforts, the ESS tool must be used to book effort.

 

1.	No more waiting period (1 week) between closure of Timecard window <https://rb-wam-ap.bosch.com/rbei-plw-prod/plw/collaboration/TimeCard%20Due%20Date%20Details>  in the BGSW effort booking tool and enablement of Effort Not Booked (ENB) window in Employee Self-Services (ESS). Eg: For CW46 (09.11.2025 to 15.11.2025), the timecard window closes on 24.11.2025 and the ENB window will be enabled on the following day, that is, by 25.11.2025
2.	All pending leave requests (except ENB, Deputation, Business reason, Forgot ID) in the manager queue pertaining to previous month corrections will be auto-approved on the early hours of 24th calendar day of the month. ONLY ENB, Deputation, Business Reason, Forgot ID should be manually approved by the manager and within the monthly cut off date (23rd) to avoid payroll and / or Hybrid office presence impact to the associate.
3.	Failure to comply will result in missed days being recorded as 'blank' days (NRF) leading to payroll processing them as Leave Without Pay (LWP) and irreversible payroll deductions for the associate.

 

Managers/Timecard controllers – Please encourage your teams to book their effort on time. In the circumstances where associates have not booked effort, please ensure that the ENB is raised well in time for you to approve by the 18th of the month. Sufficient reminders between 18th to 23rd are being sent. Failure to approve leave or ENB requests by 23rd would result in disciplinary action.

 

For more information, please refer to BEST <https://kor2vm0022.apac.bosch.com/stages/#/workspace/705/_vv/process/guidance/_uhM00DGElBCG4_Vdp-zl2A>  and Leave <https://kor2vm0022.apac.bosch.com/stages/#/workspace/705/_vv/process/guidance/_MLUlAMzscWSqMYStzJkZsA>  policies. Further clarification (if any), please reach out to your respective HR-Business Partners.

 

Your cooperation is greatly appreciated.

 

Thank you for your attention to these updates.



 

Best Regards,

BGSW/HRL-CBP
